jobs.title: Senior Manager, GEO/SEO
jobs.description:
We're so happy you're here! Thank you for checking our job out and we hope to have the chance to meet you in our interview process!

About the role

We’re hiring our first full-time owner of organic search and AI discovery across every U.S. brand: Grüns, Nütrops, Immün, Jüced, Müves, and more to come. When someone searches for what we sell, on Google or in ChatGPT, Gemini, or Perplexity, they should find us. Organic is one of our biggest levers to win first orders efficiently and cut our reliance on paid media, and you’ll build it. You’ll set the strategy and ship the work yourself, using AI agents and workflows to do what usually takes a much bigger team.

This role is part of our remote HQ! We have a fully remote, high-trust work environment - and also come together on a biannual basis for amazing off-sites where we can connect IRL.

In this role, you will:

• Own the SEO and GEO strategy and roadmap across all U.S. brands (informational, commercial, and comparison intent), prioritized by revenue impact

• Personally ship technical SEO on Shopify: crawlability, indexation, site architecture, internal linking, Core Web Vitals, structured data, redirects, and canonicals

• Make our products machine-readable, with clean product data and agent-ready pages so AI shopping assistants can find and recommend us

• Write and optimize content across PDPs, collection pages, landing pages, comparison pages, FAQs, and the blog, using AI-assisted production without losing quality or brand voice

• Act as first-line compliance on SEO content using pre-approved claims, escalate to Science & Regulatory only when content goes beyond them, and help build our claims library

• Build off-site authority through syndication, targeted link building, competitor link-gap outreach, and unlinked-mention reclamation, coordinated closely with PR

• Own organic and AI visibility reporting (non-brand traffic, rankings, organic first orders and revenue, AI share of voice, citations), set targets with Finance, and report to leadership

• Build AI agents and workflows for research, briefs, production, and audits, and partner with Ecom, CRO, Copy, Creative, PR, Paid Search, and Retail to get work shipped

We’re looking for someone who:

• Has 6-8+ years of hands-on SEO experience, doing the work yourself rather than managing agencies

• Has proven GEO/AEO results: you’ve measurably increased a brand’s visibility in AI answers and can explain exactly what moved it

• Is equally strong in traditional SEO and AI search

• Is fluent in SEO tools (Semrush, Google Search Console, GA4, a site crawler) and AI visibility tools (AthenaHQ, Profound)

• Has deep Shopify experience: theme/Liquid basics, apps, faceted navigation, duplicate content, JS rendering, and structured data implementation and validation

• Uses Claude Code (or similar) to build agents and workflows that produce more work, faster, at higher quality

• Is a strong writer and editor who balances search intent, conversion, and brand voice

• Bonus: DTC experience and time in a regulated category (supplements, food, health, or beauty)

Approach to the role:

• AI-driven: You’re obsessed with automating work and building new workflows with AI

• Hands-on builder: You do the work and ship it

• Revenue-prioritized: You pick the work that drives the most first orders and revenue, not the most traffic

• Compliance-minded: You use approved claims with confidence and know when to escalate

• Cross-functional shipper: You move work through dev, Copy, CRO, and PR, and handle shared-page tradeoffs with Ecom without friction

• Comfortable with imperfect attribution: You make strong calls without clean data or mature GEO tooling

Compensation & Benefits:

At Grüns, we’re committed to providing a competitive total compensation package — grounded in market data that considers our size, stage, industry, and location. For this role, the base salary range is $140,000 - $160,000 plus bonus depending on experience, paired with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the well-being and growth of our team.

A bit about us...

At Grüns, we believe that foundational nutrition should be simple and convenient for everyone. We're dedicated to bringing comprehensive and real nutrition to you through our gummies, formulated from 60 nutrient-dense and whole-food ingredients. Simply enjoy a grab-and-go snack pack of gummies daily whenever fits best in your schedule and wherever life takes you.

Like you, we were disappointed. There’s an infinite number of “nutrition” companies, all focused on what’s best for them — not what’s best for you. Hundreds of products to sell you on, low-quality ingredients, and small nutrient doses. We’ve seen it all.

So we decided it was time to fix it. No more choking on and popping pills like a pharmacy. No more clean-up and disgust from gross powders. And no more cobbling together handfuls to dozens of supplements. Grüns is comprehensive nutrition, made convenient and delicious.

What we care about...

Be the Best: We hold ourselves, our teams, and our partners to an incredibly high standard - and we raise the bar constantly. "We've never done this before" isn't an excuse here. It's an invitation.

Own It: We act like our name is on the door. That means taking complete ownership of outcomes, collaborating deeply, working through roadblocks - not around them - and never waiting for someone else to solve the problem. Great owners are great partners.

Drive Impact, Urgently: We measure impact, not effort. We work smart and hard, move fast, and use every tool at our disposal - including AI - to focus our energy where it matters most.

Compensation & Perks:

For every role, we aim to have highly competitive compensation and opportunity for impact and career growth.

Everyone at Grüns works hard, but we believe in wellness and balance too. We have super strong benefits coverage -- for you and your family, generous PTO, free Grüns, and a few more perks centered around health and well-being that we can't wait to tell you about!

jobs.title: Sales Development Representative
jobs.description:
This is an exciting opportunity in education-focused sales, outreach, and business development. Reporting to the Director, Galileo X Partnerships, the Sales Development Representative, Galileo X, will be a key contributor to the growth and impact of Galileo’s expanding partnership programs. In this role, you will generate leads, identify aligned school districts, charter school networks, and education providers, and build a robust pipeline of potential new camp locations and collaborators.

Why This Role Matters

By meeting communities where they are, Galileo X expands access to life-changing experiences, strengthens local partnerships, and helps close opportunity gaps. Through these collaborations, which are supported by initiatives like 21st Century Community Learning Center grants & ELO-P, we bring transformative summer and enrichment programs to new communities—especially those historically underserved or without access to high-quality summer opportunities.

You Will Be Accountable For

Lead Generation & Prospecting

• Research and identify aligned leads across districts, schools, nonprofits, cities, and youth-serving organizations
• Leverage tools like LinkedIn, Outreach, & Salesforce to build targeted lead lists
• Initiate high-volume outreach via email, phone, and social platforms to spark interest and schedule discovery calls

Outreach Strategy & Execution

• Craft compelling messages that reflect Galileo’s mission and the value of Galileo X ELO-P programming
• Tailor outreach based on regional needs and partner type
• Track and optimize outreach strategies to improve open, response, and conversion rates

Cross-Team Collaboration & Growth Support

• Partner closely with the Partnerships and Programs teams to align outreach efforts with expansion goals, bringing Galileo’s hands-on, innovative programs to new communities.
• Maintain accurate and up-to-date records in Galileo’s CRM
• Reflect on early trends and feedback to share insights that inform ongoing strategy

• 1+ years of professional experience in high-volume sales, outreach, or customer-facing role
• Background in K-12 education or youth-serving organizations, a plus
• Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to craft clear, compelling messages
• Excited to reach out to potential partners, share Galileo’s mission, and grow relationships—experience handling outreach, follow-ups, or client communications is a plus.
• Highly organized with the ability to track outreach, follow-ups, and key metrics in a CRM (e.g., Salesforce or similar)
• Tech-savvy and quick to learn new tools and platforms
• Demonstrated interest in education, youth development, or mission-driven work
• Experience using sales prospecting tools is a plus (Outreach, LinkedIn, Salesforce, etc.)
• Familiarity with outbound sales frameworks or previous BDR/SDR training is a plus

We strongly encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and experiences, and we are committed to equitable and inclusive hiring practices. If you think you have what it takes to be successful in this role, we encourage you to apply!

Work Locations

San Francisco Bay Area preferred: Employees located in the San Francisco Bay Area adhere to a hybrid office and work-from-home policy. Galileo Headquarters is located at 111 Myrtle St, Ste 300, Oakland, CA 94607.

Remote, work-from-home, location is possible in the following states: California, Colorado, Illinois, Massachusetts, Texas, North Carolina, New York, or Washington.

Schedule & Time Commitment

This is a full-time position, averaging 40 hours per week. While we prioritize work-life balance, there may be times when additional hours are necessary to meet deadlines and ensure the success of our programs. This role requires travel up to 25% to attend sales events, conferences, and partner meetings. Additionally, HQ staff are expected to visit camp locations from June through August to experience camp first-hand and support our teams on the ground.

Compensation

We anticipate total on-target compensation (including base pay and commission) for this Full-Time, exempt position to be $65,000 - $90,000 annually. This estimate is based on the preferred location in California. Exact compensation may vary and will be based on multiple factors, including geography and professional experience.

Our pay practices are guided by a commitment to equity and informed by market benchmarking and internal audits to minimize bias and ensure fairness across all roles.

Benefits

We offer comprehensive benefits that reflect our commitment to supporting diverse needs:

• No-cost medical insurance for employees (additional plans and options to add dependents available at cost)
• Vision and Dental Insurance
• 401k benefits after 1 year of employment
• Flexible Paid Time Off - time off is not limited, and we strongly recommend that employees take time off to rest and recharge.
• Unlimited free camp for your child(ren), OR two free weeks to be gifted (including AM/PM Extended Care)
• Friends and Family Discount for Galileo Camps
• Priority scholarship nominations for Galileo Camps
• Generous parental leave and extensive support with leave planning
• Employee Assistance Program, options for life insurance, and more!

Please note that our job descriptions are a summary of the typical functions of the job, not an exhaustive or comprehensive list of all possible responsibilities, tasks, and duties.

We comply with the ADA and provide reasonable accommodations that allow qualified applicants/employees to perform the essential functions of the job. To request an accommodation, contact our Human Resources team.

During the onboarding process, in accordance with applicable local and state requirements, you may be required to complete a Tuberculosis (TB) screening, background check(s), and state-mandated training(s). More details will be provided during your onboarding process.

• operate a computer (including typing, reading)
• Seeing, hearing, and speaking, both nearby and at a distance
• Use hand and fingers to help with classroom supplies and operate equipment
• Frequent standing, walking, kneeling, and sitting

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager (Email & Engagement)
jobs.location: MA - Boston - Office , US - Headquarters - Maryland - Columbia
jobs.description:
Who is Tenable?

Tenable® is the Exposure Management company. Over 40,000 organizations around the globe rely on Tenable to understand and reduce cyber risk. Our global employees support 65 percent of the Fortune 500, 50 percent of the Global 2000, and large government agencies. Come be part of our journey!

What makes Tenable such a great place to work?

Ask a member of our team and they’ll answer, “Our people!” We work together to build and innovate best-in-class cybersecurity solutions for our customers; all while creating a culture of belonging, respect, and excellence where we can be our best selves. When you’re part of our #OneTenable team, you can expect to partner with some of the most talented and passionate people in the industry, and have the support and resources you need to do work that truly matters. We deliver results that exceed expectations and we win together!

Your Role:

As the Lifecycle Marketing Manager at Tenable, you will execute a global strategy for our go-to-market and lifecycle communications including email, in-product, and other communication channels. You’ll engage our core audiences, including customers, prospects and partners.

You’ll design email programs, manage customer lifecycle communications and build key market communications - all within an overarching strategy to drive pipeline, adoption, and retention.

The ideal candidate is an experienced communications professional who brings a strategic mindset along with experience designing email marketing programs, managing customer engagement programs, and working across global teams. The Lifecycle Marketing Manager will be the champion of Tenable’s email voice and strategy, working to establish and maintain a consistent voice across regions. Strong copywriting skills will be essential to help write compelling emails and adapt messaging for key personas (Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs), IT leaders, and practitioners in the cybersecurity industry) across various communication channels.

Your Opportunity:

• Lifecycle Communication Strategy: Own messaging strategy across email (including newsletters, customer notifications, lead nurture campaigns, product launches, global events, and more), in-product messaging, and other communication channels.

• Program Execution: Support engagement programs such as virtual events, community engagement, and advocacy programs.

• Copywriting and Editing: Draft, refine and edit high-converting copy for a wide range of types of email communications and messaging. Ensure a consistent tone of voice across all communications.

• Persona-Based Targeting: Adapt strategy and messaging for different buyer personas, aligning to prospect and customer lifecycles to effectively nurture leads and fuel customer growth.

• A/B Testing: Design and manage ongoing A/B tests across email copy, schedules and layouts. Apply learnings to optimize and adjust email strategy.

• Project Management: Balance many projects simultaneously with short deadlines. Maintain a global communication calendar and provide visibility to key stakeholders.

• Global Partnership: Serve as a global bridge across regional marketing teams. Create and maintain global email standards to maintain a consistent style and voice across regions and audiences.

• Reporting & Analytics: Track KPIs, analyze engagement metrics and performance against demand generation goals, and present insights to key stakeholders.

What You’ll Need:

• 5+ years of professional experience in email marketing, demand generation, or lifecycle marketing.

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

• Ability to provide an email writing sample showcasing how you adapt tone and messaging for different persona types (requested at the hiring manager stage).

• A clear understanding of email strategy, what constitutes a successful campaign and how to measure and improve performance.

jobs.title: Senior Director / Executive Director, Forecasting & New Product Planning
jobs.description:
ARS Pharmaceuticals is a fast-growing, innovative company dedicated to transforming the treatment of severe allergic reactions with neffy®, the first and only FDA-approved needle-free epinephrine product. If you’re motivated to make a meaningful impact, this is your opportunity to join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and inclusive culture.

JOB SUMMARY:

Reporting to the Chief Commercial Officer, the Sr. Director/Executive Director, Forecasting & Commercial Assessments is the company’s authoritative source for commercial projections and strategic market analytics. This leader owns the corporate forecast for neffy, leads commercial assessments for neffy lifecycle opportunities and future pipeline and business development assets, and directs the Market Insights and Competitive Intelligence function through an experienced Senior Director.

The role is a strategic analytical partner to the CCO and the executive leadership team. It turns market data, performance trends, and forward-looking assumptions into the commercial story the company presents to its Board of Directors and the investment community.

This is a high-visibility role for a leader who can build a rigorous, defensible model, leading to a clear, confident point of view for senior executives, investors and the Board. Success depends on close collaboration with Marketing, Sales, Market Access, Commercial Operations, Trade/Channel, Finance, Medical Affairs, Investor Relations and Business Development, and will be demonstrated through the actions and deliverables below.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Forecasting & Commercial Assessment

• Own the corporate demand forecast for neffy; the number used for the operating plan, S&OP, and external guidance, including scenario and sensitivity analysis

• Provide the forecast foundation that Commercial Operations uses for quota setting, incentive compensation design, and territory-level planning

• Track actual performance against forecast and lead variance analysis. Define leading indicators such as prescription trends, new-to-brand and refill behavior, and gross-to-net, and recalibrate assumptions as the market develops.

• Assist with commercial assessments for pipeline opportunities and business development targets, covering addressable patient population, pricing and access assumptions, peak sales, and risk-adjusted value

• Support diligence on in-licensing and M&A opportunities with rapid, decision-grade analysis

Market insights & Competitive Intelligence

• Lead the Market Insights and CI function through the Senior Director, setting the research agenda, priorities and budget to align with forecasting, brand planning and leadership decision needs.

• Ensure primary research directly informs forecast assumptions and strategic choices, including demand studies, ATU tracking, conjoint and pricing research, and HCP, patient, caregiver and payer research

• Oversee competitive monitoring, scenario planning and war-gaming to anticipate competitor actions and market shifts and prepare the organization to respond

Board and Investor Narrative

• Serve as the analytical lead behind Board materials, earnings preparation, guidance discussions and investor events, keeping the external narrative consistent with the internal forecast

• Work with the CFO and Investor Relations to prepare data-backed responses to investor and analyst questions. Monitor sell-side consensus models and explain where and why company views differ

• Translate complex analyses into clear, executive-ready visuals and messages that make the commercial story easy to follow

Cross-Functional Partnership and Team Leadership

• Act as a trusted colleague and thought partner to commercial leaders and promote data driven decision-making across the organization.

• Maintain a single, aligned view of the market and forecast so that leadership, the Board and investors all receive consistent numbers.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

• Bachelor’s degree in business or related discipline required; MBA/advanced degree preferred. Equivalent combination of education and relevant job experience may be considered

• 15+ years of related experience, with a minimum of 8 years in Life Sciences - biotechnology, pharmaceuticals or a related field

• Prior experience and expert knowledge within commercial disciplines such as forecasting/analytics, product strategy, new product planning, market research, pricing, or strategic marketing

• Demonstrated experience providing key commercial insights, pipeline planning & forecasting, and leading the insights function to relate scientific information & market intelligence into commercial recommendations

• Experience successfully partnering across the organization to align and move efforts forward

• Demonstrated experience in presenting complex data, strategies, and concepts to key stakeholders/executive team/Board

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

• Strong quantitative and analytical skills, including the ability to evaluate forecasts, market models and commercial scenarios

• Solid understanding of pharmaceutical development and end-to-end commercialization

• Proven ability to lead cross-functional projects/teams, and collaborate well and influence without direct authority

• Strong judgment in situations involving ambiguity or incomplete information

• Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills with the ability to communicate clear, decision-oriented recommendations

• Entrepreneurial, hands-on operating style suited to a fast-paced biotechnology environment

• Collaborative, influential, and excellent people skills

• Ability to travel up to 30% is required for success in the role

LEVELING SENIOR DIRECTOR/EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR:
The role will be leveled based on the candidate’s experience, scope of prior leadership, and readiness to operate independently with the Board and investors, as determined by ARS. Both levels own the same core responsibilities; the Executive Director level carries greater autonomy, external exposure and enterprise influence.

At ARS, we are proud to offer a highly competitive compensation & benefits package.

The full-time salary range for this posted position is $285,000 to $320,000 and may be eligible for a discretionary annual performance bonus. Actual pay rates are determined by considering multiple factors including qualifications, relevance of experience, education & credentials, subject matter expertise, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

This position is also eligible for Equity, 401k matching, and our excellent benefits package including 100% employer paid Medical, Dental & Vision for employees. View the full package here: ARS Careers Page

ARS Pharmaceuticals is also committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals so that an individual can perform their job-related duties. If you are interested in applying for an employment opportunity and require special assistance or an accommodation to apply due to a disability, please contact us at careers@ars-pharma.com

jobs.title: Senior People Operations Coordinator, Claude Corps
jobs.description:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. Our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. After nearly a decade of training technical talent, we launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic to prepare people for careers in AI.

We're expanding into new markets and growing our team as AI changes the workforce. People joining CodePath now will help shape this next stage of our work.

We believe technical skills create opportunities. Our goal is to train millions of learners and create lasting economic impact. If you want to build something new, take ownership, and see the results of your work, this is a place to do it.

Location: Remote (US)
Role Type: Full-Time
Reporting to: Senior HR Business Partner, Claude Corps
Compensation: $65,000 to $85,000

About Claude Corps

Claude Corps is a fellowship that places early-career talent in nonprofits, government agencies, and public-interest organizations to build AI solutions those organizations can continue using after the fellowship ends. It is a partnership between Anthropic, CodePath, and Social Finance. Fellows are full-time employees for a one-year term.

Cohorts now run in the hundreds, and new fellows onboard while earlier cohorts are still placed. We need a coordinator who can run the day-to-day onboarding work at that scale, in partnership with the Senior HR Business Partner, and make sure every step is organized, accurate, and completed on time.

About the Role

You run the day-to-day onboarding work for Claude Corps fellows, from signed offer through completion of required employment steps. You send instructions, track progress, maintain employee records, and coordinate payroll and benefits setup.

The Senior HR Business Partner owns the overall onboarding process and handles sensitive questions and exceptions. You complete the work, keep fellows informed, and flag issues early.

You work closely with recruiting, the Claude Corps program team, Finance, and our HR service providers. Between onboarding waves, you help maintain records, coordinate offboarding, and improve processes so the team is ready for the next cohort.

What You’ll Do

Coordinate fellow onboarding

• Manage onboarding for each cohort, including offer tracking, background checks, I-9 verification, employee information collection, HRIS setup in CoAdvantage, and benefits enrollment

• Track required employment steps and deadlines, ensuring fellows are ready to start on time and records are complete and accurate

• Maintain a centralized onboarding tracker, proactively identifying outstanding items, potential delays, and issues requiring escalation

• Coordinate with Finance on onboarding clearances and flag sensitive or compliance-related concerns to the Senior HR Business Partner

Be the primary point of contact for fellows

• Serve as the primary point of contact for onboarding questions, providing timely, clear, and supportive communication

• Send onboarding instructions, reminders, and updates so fellows understand what to expect and what actions they need to take

• Resolve routine questions and coordinate with the appropriate HR partners on benefits, system issues, or policy-related matters

• Manage the HR inbox with care, discretion, and consistent follow-through

Maintain systems and improve processes

• Keep employee records, onboarding trackers, process documentation, the Notion hub, and relevant Fellow Handbook resources accurate and up to date

• Support offboarding and ongoing employee record maintenance between onboarding cohorts

• Create clear, repeatable workflows that support larger cohorts and allow additional team members to step in when needed

• Use AI and automation to reduce repetitive work, improve efficiency, and maintain accuracy as the program grows

Requirements

• Experience coordinating high-volume onboarding, people operations, or HR processes with time-sensitive requirements

• Familiarity with HRIS or PEO systems and the ability to learn new tools quickly

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with experience maintaining accurate records, trackers, and deadlines

• Clear, warm communication skills and a commitment to creating a positive employee experience

• Sound judgment when handling confidential information, resolving questions, and escalating sensitive matters

• Experience using AI or automation tools to improve workflows and reduce manual work

• A proactive, service-oriented approach and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment

Key Success Metrics

• Onboarding Readiness: Fellows complete required employment steps accurately and on time, with payroll and benefits information ready for their start dates

• Fellow Experience: Fellows receive clear instructions, timely updates, and responsive support throughout onboarding

• Operational Accuracy: Employee records and onboarding trackers remain current, with potential issues identified and communicated early

• Efficiency and Collaboration: Teams receive timely information, and onboarding processes become more consistent and efficient as cohorts grow

Compensation

CodePath has standardized salaries based on the position’s level, no matter where you live. For this role, we’re offering an annual salary of $65,000 to $85,000. Salary is determined based on your relevant experience and skills as evaluated through our interview process.

Full-Time Employee Benefits

This is a remote position—work from anywhere in the US! CodePath prioritizes employee well-being with a competitive benefits package to support your health, financial security, and work-life balance.

• Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance (90% employer-covered for employees and dependents), employer-funded healthcare reimbursement, FSAs, and Employee Assistance Program

• Financial Security: 401(k), employer-paid life & disability insurance, and identity theft protection

• Work-Life Balance: Generous PTO, paid holidays, 10 weeks of fully paid parental leave, and an annual year-end company closure (Dec 24 – Jan 2)

• Professional Growth: $1,000 annual professional development stipend and home office setup support

• ​​Student Loan Forgiveness: CodePath is a qualifying employer for Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), helping employees manage student loan debt

• Additional Perks: Pet wellness plans, legal services, home/auto insurance discounts, and exclusive marketplace savings

Pay range

$65,000—$85,000 USD

jobs.title: Site Reliability Engineer 2 - Production Engineering
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Production Engineering team is a newly formed organization within Anduril's Software Platform, dedicated to the reliability, performance, and scalability of the cloud infrastructure behind Lattice, Anduril's autonomous command and control platform. Our work helps keep mission-critical systems available in demanding operational environments.

Our team operates at the intersection of software engineering and systems reliability. We run on-call and incident management tooling, build observability and automation, and create the playbooks that help teams detect and recover from production issues. We partner with engineering teams across Anduril as a force multiplier: we provide the platform and operational support, while product teams retain ownership of their services.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Site Reliability Engineer 2 who is passionate about building resilient, highly available systems that scale to meet the demands of the core systems powering Lattice. You will work closely with platform engineers, product developers, and field operations to proactively identify reliability risks, respond to incidents, and help owning teams improve the operational excellence of our software platform. This is a hands-on role on a growing team, with opportunities to build shared tooling and processes that make reliability improvements easier to deliver. If you thrive on solving hard problems and want your work to have a direct impact on national security, this is the role for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Build and improve monitoring, observability, and alerting systems to detect reliability issues early and make them easier to diagnose across the Lattice platform

• Participate in on-call rotations, triage production incidents, and coordinate response and escalation with the teams that own affected services

• Contribute to blameless postmortems and work with owning teams to turn incident learnings into systemic improvements

• Build and maintain shared reliability tooling and automation that reduce toil, surface risks, and help teams make safer changes

• Partner with service owners to identify Kubernetes patch and version risks, develop maintenance plans, and track owner-led updates to completion

• Help service teams define and track Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets to balance feature velocity with reliability

• Partner with software engineering teams on reliability patterns such as graceful degradation and circuit breakers

• Contribute to capacity planning and performance testing with owning teams to help systems handle growth and peak operational demands

• Create runbooks, documentation, and training materials that help teams operate production systems effectively

• Partner with software engineering teams to improve deployment safety through progressive rollouts, automated testing, and rollback capabilities

• Work with service owners to incorporate security best practices and compliance controls in production environments handling sensitive defense data

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 2-4 years of engineering experience, including 2+ years in SRE, production operations, or infrastructure engineering

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

• Hands-on experience troubleshooting Kubernetes in production, with an understanding of version lifecycles, patching, and ongoing operational risks

• Strong programming skills in one or more languages such as Go, Python, Rust, or Java, with the ability to build production-grade tooling

• Experience building and using observability tooling for metrics, logging, and tracing, such as Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, or equivalent

• Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and infrastructure as code practices, preferably Terraform

• Ability to troubleshoot distributed systems issues across multiple layers of the stack and work with owning teams on durable fixes

• Strong incident management and communication skills

• Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

• Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience with defense, aerospace, or other mission-critical systems where downtime has severe consequences

• Familiarity with performance optimization and capacity planning for high-throughput, low-latency systems

• Knowledge of chaos engineering principles and experience with resilience testing

• Experience with Kubernetes ingress and traffic management (Gateway API, Contour, or similar)

• Familiarity with GitOps and deployment automation (ArgoCD, FluxCD) and CI build infrastructure (CircleCI, Nix, or similar)

• Experience with Terraform workflows at scale, including module design and PR-based automation (Atlantis or similar)

• Experience with incident and alerting tooling such as PagerDuty, Datadog, or Groundcover

• Understanding of networking fundamentals including load balancing, DNS, TLS/SSL, and network security

• Experience with configuration management and secrets management solutions

• Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders

• Active Secret or higher security clearance

US Salary Range

$147,000—$185,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: H&M Department Manager - Washington Square
jobs.description:
About the Role

As a Department Manager, you’ll be the leader supporting and encouraging your whole team. By bringing everyone together, you’ll be able to create an inclusive culture that promotes collaboration and an entrepreneurial spirit, helping you, your team, and H&M succeed. Ensuring an excellent operational & visual experience for your store, customers & colleagues. You’ll be aware of your store’s strengths, opportunities, and competitors. Analyze and follow up on sales, and create plans to optimize results and profits.

A Day in the Life

Working at H&M means no two days are ever the same, but a typical day will include the following responsibilities*

Customer Sales & Profit

• You are responsible for the total OMNI customer experience in your store, ensuring visual and commercial curation according to global guidelines
• Representing yourself and the H&M brand positively during customer interactions
• Be aware of and take responsibility of your department's strengths and identifying commercial opportunities and acting on them
• Establish & analyze sales and budget goals, creating plans to optimize results
• Ensure customer service is provided in all areas of the store and that your team has the ability to work towards actively promoting and selling products to customers
• Following up that your team is actively promoting our Customer Loyalty App (Hello Member) & in-store sustainability initiatives
• Manage your department in a cost-efficient way
• Ensure correct routines in fitting room and checkout, including transaction, returns and exchanges
• Ensure all admin routines for both people and operations are handled in a correct way

Fashion & Trend Awareness

• Keep up-to-date with fashion scene, trends, tendencies, styles, brands, products, competitors and relevant influencers, etc
• Ensure your team provides product and fashion knowledge as well as other relevant information during customer interactions

Team & Development

• Responsible for recruitment, onboarding, performance management, upskilling & developing your team in-store
• Complete performance evaluations and succession planning to support business & team needs
• Retain and share your knowledge and skills with your team
• Collaboration, planning & teamwork with in-store Visual Merchandiser team
• Give & receive feedback with your colleagues to learn, develop & support each other
• Responsible for the teams planning & scheduling
• Regular communication to store colleagues to inform, motivate and inspire – daily, weekly meetings, etc
• Ensure all procedures, routines, and legal requirements in all areas of the store are followed
• Participate in relevant available Onboarding & introduction processes, trainings and courses relevant for your role & future development

Retail Operations/ Visual & Commercial Execution

• Secure a clean and tidy sales floor and back of house including stockroom areas
• Ensure high fashion quality, visual and commercial product presentation, with good garment care
• Secure good stock levels and provide input on allocation to Area team
• Ensure the full garment cycle – from delivery to garment presentation – and fitting room routines are according to our standards and routines set internally, utilizing all tools and technology provided
• Upkeep & follow best practice for any in-store OMNI Services & in-store tech services/tools, etc (Instore Care App, Click & Collect, Smart Store etc)
• Secure a strong balance and the maintenance of price signs in-store and throughout the sales floor/store following guidelines according to global and local strategies & sales market/regional requirements to ensure a strong and consistent price perception throughout store
• Updating & upkeep of BOH Areas for all colleagues (key information, health & safety, tidiness etc)
• Responsible for opening & closing of store daily

Who You Are

• To be a successful and effective Department Manager, you’ll be a strong leader who enjoys taking responsibility for others.
• You must be ambitious, an effective communicator, supportive, an analytical solution finder, capable of working with numbers and managing statistics.
• You are achievement-oriented, motivated by performance and competition to be truly customer centric.

Why You’ll Love Working at H&M

• We value diverse backgrounds, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, and disability
• We pride ourselves on being a values-driven organization, guided by our 7 unique values that have been part of our success story for over 75 years
• You’ll have access to our Colleague Resource Groups (CRGs) to find community and networking opportunities among colleagues
• We are an inclusive company where you’re encouraged to be yourself at work
• You will have access to a large global talent community, where career growth and aspirations have no limits
• We believe in supporting your overall wellbeing and offer comprehensive benefits inclusive of health insurance, wellness and family support programs, company match retirement plan, paid leave programs, and paid time off, including a community day to serve your local community

Inclusion & Diversity:

H&M is a part of H&M Group. At H&M Group, we’re determined to create and maintain inclusive, diverse and equitable workplaces throughout our organisation. Having a diverse workforce leads to a positive impact on how we address challenges, on what we perceive possible and on how we choose to relate to our colleagues and customers all over the world. Hence all diversity dimensions are taken into consideration in our recruitment process.

We strive to have a fair and equal process and therefore kindly ask you not to attach a cover letter in your application as they often contain information that easily can trigger unintentional biases.

Company Description:

At H&M, our purpose is to liberate fashion for the many. We want to shape a new world in Fashion. A world with one ultimate goal: to unleash your self-expression. As an H&M colleague, you’re encouraged to be yourself & more. You’ll take on new responsibilities from day one, learn skills for life, and find new ways to make your big dreams come true.

jobs.title: Senior Financial Analyst
jobs.description:
Senior Financial Analyst Include but are not Limited to the Following:

The Senior Financial Analyst will assume end-to-end ownership of the organization’s financial performance, serving as a strategic partner to senior leadership. This role is responsible for analyzing key financial and operational metrics, developing scalable and dynamic financial models, and delivering actionable insights that support data-driven decision-making and long-term growth.

In addition to core FP&A responsibilities, this position will lead the design and implementation of a structured, disciplined collections process to optimize cash flow and ensure timely client payments. The ideal candidate brings a proactive, solution-oriented mindset, strong analytical rigor, and the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders to drive performance and accountability.

• Financial Reporting & Analysis:Prepare, review, and analyze monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow) for accuracy and insights.Generate regular reporting on operational and financial KPIs, highlighting trends and opportunities for improvement.Conduct variance analysis including volume, mix, and margin trends to identify deviations from budgets and forecasts and propose corrective measures.Support M&A activities through financial analysis, due diligence, and valuation. Lead post-acquisition financial integration, ensuring alignment of reporting structures, processes, and performance tracking.Ensure compliance with relevant accounting standards and company policies; recommend and implement internal controls where needed.

• Budgeting & Forecasting:Lead the annual budgeting process, working with department heads to develop realistic, data-driven budgets and ensure alignment with strategic goals.Build and maintain financial models to project cash flow, revenue, and profitability; monitor performance against these forecasts.Develop forward-looking financial scenarios that incorporate market trends, growth assumptions, and operational drivers to support executive decision-making.
• Business Partnering & Strategic Support:Collaborate across business segments and functions to provide financial guidance on key business decisions and initiatives.Build relationships across centralized functions and accounting to ensure accurate reporting and effective financial management.Perform in-depth profitability and cost analyses to identify cost savings, process improvements, and investment opportunities.Present management reporting packages to executive leadership, contributing to long-term strategic planning.
• Working Capital Management:Identify and recommend process improvements in financial operations, including billing, collections, and reporting, to improve efficiency and accuracy.Monitor accounts receivable aging, proactively address outstanding balances and billing discrepancies, identify risks and process improvements, and report on cash flow impacts to support timely client payments and strengthen liquidity.Partner with business and functional stakeholders to optimize procure-to-pay processes, enhance internal controls, and ensure accurate, timely execution across purchasing and payment workflows
• Ad Hoc Projects & Leadership:Lead or support high-impact financial and operational projects while proactively identifying finance capability gaps.Contribute to the development of the finance organization, ensuring the appropriate structure, tools, and talent are in place to support business growth.

Basic Minimum Education Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or related field; MBA preferred.

jobs.title: Associate Regional Director - North
jobs.description:
CBEM brings lasting, positive changes to the individuals with developmental disabilities we serve, some of whom experience mental illness. Our process begins with observations from which we design a comprehensive plan. It continues on as we teach our clients and their circle of support how to obtain positive, sustainable outcomes.

Job Title: Associate Regional Director

Position Reports to: Regional Director

Job Classification: Exempt

Region: Hybrid, Must live in the North Region

Location: Hybrid / Remote (This person must live in Northern California and be able to regularly travel by car to all sites.)

Compensation: $102,500 + opportunities for quarterly bonus

Position Summary:

The Associate Regional Director is a key operational leadership role responsible for ensuring high-quality, compliant, and consistent service delivery across a defined geographic region of CBEM offices. This position provides direct coaching, oversight, and accountability to Program Directors and ensures that Program Design, Policies & Procedures, contractual requirements, and quality standards are implemented with fidelity.

The Associate Regional Director strengthens stakeholder relationships, drives local outreach efforts, improves KPI performance, and ensures operational readiness for audits, expansion, and contractual reviews. A primary function of the role is regional travel to each office at least twice per quarter to conduct observations, assess compliance, support leadership development, and serve as a liaison between CBEM leadership and field operations. Other travel may be required.

The Associate Regional Director is also required to obtain and maintain certification as a crisis intervention instructor (e.g., Pro-ACT, QBS Safety-Care, CPI, or equivalent) to lead and model high-quality crisis prevention and intervention training for staff across assigned offices.

This role ensures operational stability by providing short-term coverage for Program Director or Assistant Director vacancies through modeling CBEM’s values of consistency, professionalism, and collaborative problem-solving. The Associate Regional Director may assume the Administrator on Call rotation when needed.

Essential Duties include, but are not limited to:

Operations Visits & Check-Ins

• Completes two on-site visits per quarter.

• Completes biweekly check-ins with the Program Directors, or more if needed.

Program & Policy Compliance

• Ensures all offices adhere to Program Designs, contractual requirements, Title 17, internal Policies & Procedures, and CBEM’s service fidelity model.

• Conducts two onsite visits quarterly per office to monitor and assess compliance, conduct observations, and build rapport with the team.

• Collaborates with the Regional Director and the QA team to close compliance gaps, monitor deadlines, and validate corrective actions.

• Trains Program Directors and leadership teams in interpreting and implementing Program Designs and agency policies.

• Ensures consistent application of Introductory Period Documents, processes, training mandates, safety protocols, and workforce compliance standards.

• Facilitates annual AOC training under the direction of Regional Leadership.

• Facilitates annual Operations Manual training to ensure fidelity.

• Ensures documentation compliance, PVF/POS fidelity, employee file audits, weekly billing projections, and baseline KPI maintenance.

Operational Leadership and Support

• Provides direct operational guidance to Program Directors, enabling them to prioritize leadership and client-outcome work.

• Reviews, approves, and monitors billing reports, payroll submissions, and reimbursement requests for accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with CBEM’s financial and operational policies.

• Ensures adherence to CBEM’s budgetary expectations, spending guidelines, and operational reimbursement policies across assigned offices.

• Observes and enforces compliance with mileage submission requirements, verifying alignment with CBEM’s mileage policy and ensuring that all submissions are timely, accurate, and consistent with travel expectations.

• Develops and manages the Administrator On-Call schedule to ensure appropriate coverage. Monitors crisis line operations for compliance and provides coaching and development to Program Directors to strengthen crisis response quality.

• Acts as the office-level “troubleshooter” to resolve operational barriers quickly and reduce risks impacting service delivery.

• Ensures consistency in KPI performance through monitoring, coaching, and standardized office practices.

• Consolidates program-level data for Regional Director review; ensures accuracy and timely reporting.

• Operationally prepares offices for expansions, launches of new service lines, and integration of new staff.

Serves as Interim Program Director or Assistant Director when vacancies require coverage to maintain continuity and stability.Stakeholder Engagement & Outreach

• Ensures Program Directors execute local outreach plans aligned with Regional Center expectations, crisis service needs, and community engagement goals.

• Attends outreach events, vendor meetings, presentations, and stakeholder engagements to strengthen the CBEM brand.

• Builds and maintains strong relationships with Regional Center liaisons, service providers, law enforcement, and community partners.

• Ensures consistent messaging, professionalism, and follow-through on stakeholder needs.

• Partners with the Regional Director to elevate concerns, trends, or opportunities arising from stakeholder interactions.

• Manages office-level outreach plans and analyzes quarterly outreach data to support regional outreach goals.

Team Development & Leadership Pipeline

• Coaches, supervises, and mentors Program Directors, promoting leadership growth, confidence, and accountability.

• Identifies emerging leaders and collaborates with regional leadership on succession planning.

• Provides training, modeling, and skill development in crisis intervention, operational efficiency, and compliance execution.

• Ensures mandated training, compliance modules, supervision structures, and DIPET expectations are followed by office staff.

• Facilitates model fidelity audits to ensure compliance and oversees their compliance at the Program Director level.

• Reviews Program Directors’ Professional Development Plans monthly and provides coaching aligned to regional goals.

• Collaborates with Regional Leadership to contribute to succession planning through the identification and review of emerging leaders.

• Collaborates with QA and Clinical Leadership to update agency training modules based on regional needs and compliance findings.

Travel, Observations, and Onsite Support

• Travels to each office at least two times per quarter for observations, coaching, compliance reviews, and relationship building.

• Conducts in-person walkthroughs, crisis response assessments, staff observations, and operational evaluations.

• Builds trust and cohesion between field teams and CBEM leadership, serving as a primary liaison.

• Supports offices during high-risk events, staffing transitions, or operational challenges requiring onsite leadership.

Other Responsibilities

• Participates in leadership meetings, strategic planning efforts, and interdepartmental work groups when invited.

• Completes required documentation, reports, coaching logs, and follow-up summaries.

• Performs additional duties as assigned by the Regional Director or Operations leadership.

Qualifications

Requirements the Candidate must have.

Education

• A Master’s degree from a four-year college or university in psychology, social work, or behavioral science is preferred. Still, a Bachelor's degree with extensive experience in crisis intervention/behavioral health and experience leading teams is required.

Experience

• At least two years of experience managing a team is required. At least one year of experience working at CBEM, with a track record of displaying leadership qualities of empowerment, critical thinking, facilitating fair and consistent practices, cultural alignment, and the ability to meet or exceed company-wide goals.

• Strong working knowledge of Developmental Disabilities.

• Strong working knowledge of the Department of Developmental Disabilities, Regional Centers, and the Lanterman Act.

• Strong working knowledge of navigating social services systems to support new service lines.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Demonstrated experience working with individuals with developmental disabilities.

• Demonstrated leadership capabilities.

Physical Demands

• The physical demands described here are representative of those required of an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

• While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to walk, sit, stand, and drive. The employee is also required to use their hands and reach with their arms. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and the ability to adjust focus. <The employee may be required to occasionally intervene in physically demanding behavioral interventions with physically aggressive clients.

License/Certification

• Current California driver’s license and proof of sufficient car insurance minimums (must be maintained during employment)

• Clearance of DOJ/FBI records (complete before hire)

• Proof of Negative Tuberculosis Screening (upon hire)

Mandatory Training Requirements

• Operations Manual Training

• Administrator on Call Training

• Clinical Module Training

• CPR/First Aid Certifications (complete during employment). Maintain CPR/First Aid Certifications.

• Bloodborne Pathogen Training (complete during employment)

• Driver Safety Training (complete during employment)

• Harassment and Discrimination Prevention Training (complete during employment)

• Additional training as required and assigned.

• Monthly Safety Trainings

Skills, Knowledge, Abilities

What the Candidate must be able to do in the role.

Behavioral/Clinical Skills

• Expertise in crisis prevention, least-restrictive strategies, behavioral programming, and trauma-informed care.

• Ability to train and develop leaders to provide interventions that incorporate empathy, compassion, positive behavioral programming, respect, openness, and a client-centered approach.

• Ability to de-escalate crises, model calm communication, and coach staff through complex cases.

• Strong understanding of Title 17, Positive Behavioral Programming, and co-occurring mental health needs.

• Operates as a self-starter with a high degree of independence, requiring minimal direction to identify priorities, initiate solutions, and overcome complex obstacles. Demonstrates the tenacity and follow-through required to drive strategic objectives to completion, actively modeling critical thinking and self-directed problem-solving for all staff.

Writing & Communication Skills

• Ability to write professional emails, coaching logs, compliance reports, and stakeholder communication.

• Able to communicate effectively with Regional Centers, community partners, and internal teams.

• Reasoning & Problem-Solving

• Skilled at analyzing operational barriers and designing actionable solutions.

• Comfortable interpreting policies, procedures, diagrams, and workflows.

Technical Skills

• Proficient with Mac/Apple systems and CBEM’s Critical Intervention Service database.

• Proficient with Google Suite.

• Able to manage multiple priorities and deadlines independently.

Core Competencies

How the Candidate behaves and performs in this role.

Operational & Program Oversight Multi-Site Management:
Oversees multiple locations, ensuring consistency, efficiency, and high-quality service delivery across the region.

Compliance & Risk Management:
Ensures all programs operate in full adherence to legal, ethical, contractual, and organizational policies and procedures.Performance & Outcomes Monitoring: Uses KPIs, metrics, and operational data to evaluate program effectiveness and implement measurable improvements.

Leadership & Talent Development Leadership Development:
Coaches and mentors Program Directors, Assistant Directors, and emerging leaders to strengthen CBEM’s internal leadership pipeline.

Team Engagement & Culture:
Fosters a positive, inclusive, accountable, and high-performing workplace culture that promotes staff retention and professional growth.

Crisis & Risk Management Resilience & Stress Management:
Provides steady guidance and support to teams navigating high-pressure, crisis-oriented environments. Demonstrates calm leadership and models sound decision-making.Strategic Leadership & Vision Organizational Strategy: Aligns regional operations with CBEM’s mission, values, and long-term strategic priorities.Change Management: Leads teams through organizational transitions, policy updates, new initiatives, and service expansions, ensuring smooth adaptation and consistent implementation.

jobs.title: Senior Cell Assay Support Specialists
jobs.description:
The Senior Cell Assay Support Specialists is primarily responsible for providing pre- and post- sale technical support, of cellular and biochemical assay products, to customers globally. The employee will work from an office in Fremont, California. The employee will independently assess the needs/issues of clients and determine the best course of action to support them, which can include remotely troubleshooting assays, providing technical information about products (cell assay and other reagents), assay protocol information and guidance, and providing technical documents.

The employee will also provide feedback to the business to help drive product improvements and be a key member of a committee that review product issues and drives the company’s product improvement program.  The employee will support the Product Management team by reviewing product documents in development or revision (e.g. user manuals and product datasheets) to ensure that the accurate information is available to customers.

The employee will also assist with development and maintenance of customer case management tools.  At times, the employee will also support other customer support team and sales team members and assist with training of other technical support personnel.

Senior Cell Assay Support Specialists Duties Include but are not Limited to the Following:

• Serves as primary contact for pre- and post-sale technical support through email, phone and telelconference calls.
• Provides support for all Eurofins DiscoverX Products to global customers and sales staff.
• Troubleshoot customer issues, which can include coordinating and tracking preliminary investigations of product performance with the reagent manufacturing and/or R&D teams.
• Participate in web conference calls with customers for both pre- and post- sale support.
• Coordinates with customer service team to issue product replacements to customers when necessary.
• Contribute technical support team’s knowledge database. Follows procedures to ensure adequate inquiry and complaint handling; documents inquiries and complaint resolutions in the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) case management system.
• Assist with the development and maintenance management of the technical support team’s case management system.
• Proactively report/record product problems/issues into the company’s product improvement tracking system. Collaborate with the Quality Assurance (QA) team as a member of the committee manages this product improvement program.
• Assists the Technical Support Manager with quarterly reporting of the team’s activities the Eurofins DiscoverX Products management and to the Product Management, Market Development, QA, regent manufacturing and Operations teams.
• Escalates critical complaints to Product Managers, Operations, and Quality Assurance as necessary.
• Assists the Products commercial team with the development or revisions of product documentation (e.g. user manuals and product datasheets).
• Assists the manager with reviews and approvals of change orders required of the technical support team.
• Assists Technical Support Manager with establishment, and continuous improvement of Technical Support SOPs; assist with the development of technical support team’s procedures.
• May occasionally be asked to travel to assist the marketing team at trade shows (i.e. represent the company at exhibit booths; presenting scientific posters)
• Supports other technical support personnel, including junior support representatives and regional representatives and field application scientists.
• Assists with training of other technical support representatives.
• Some lab work for training will be required
• Demonstrates and promotes the company vision
• Regular attendance and punctuality
• Conducts all activities in a safe and efficient manner
• Performs other duties as assigned
• Owns the accountability and responsibility of delivering to client needs and timeliness
• Provides cross-functional support to other departments as required
• Adjusts work hours as needed to meet client deadlines
• Adheres to site employee health and safety (EHS) requirements
• Some travel to other business units, primarily for training purposes, may be require

Basic Minimum Education Qualifications:

• PhD/MS in cell biology, pharmacology or a related discipline,

Basic Minimum Work Requirements:

• Minimum 1 -2 years (for PhD) or 2 - 4 years (for MS) of experience with cell-based assays.
• Experience with assay development, particularly cell-based assays.

As a strategic partner to Commercial and Finance leadership, this role translates market dynamics and business performance into forecast assumptions and recommendations that inform decision-making.

This role manages forecasting deliverables across annual planning, Latest Best Estimate (LBE), Long-Range Plan (LRP), portfolio planning, and actuals reporting, working closely with Commercial, Marketing, Pricing, Market Analytics, Business Insights, and Finance partners.

The successful candidate combines financial and analytical expertise with business acumen, clear communication, and the ability to influence cross-functional teams.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and deliver commercial sales and volume forecasts for the immunology portfolio across annual planning, LBE, LRP, portfolio planning, and actuals reporting.
• Build and document forecast assumptions using market dynamics, competitive intelligence, historical performance, patient and demand trends, and pricing considerations.
• Evaluate business scenarios, risks, and opportunities, and communicate forecast methodologies, key changes, and recommendations to Commercial and Finance leadership.
• Support month-end close through demand variance analysis, performance assessment, and concise management commentary.
• Provide ad hoc forecasting and analytical support for emerging business needs, strategic initiatives, and leadership requests.
• Improve forecast accuracy, analytical quality, efficiency, and transparency through enhanced processes, methodologies, and tools.
• Support the adoption of forecasting systems through training, process documentation, change management, and cross-functional alignment.
• Maintain data integrity and comply with AbbVie financial policies, internal controls, and reporting requirements.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, Analytics, or a related field required.
• Minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in commercial finance, sales or demand forecasting, financial planning and analysis, revenue forecasting, business analytics, financial reporting, or a related discipline.
• Demonstrated ability to develop, manage, and communicate complex sales or demand forecasts using sound analytical assumptions and structured methodologies.
• Strong financial modeling, analytical, technical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex information and identify meaningful business insights.
• Strong business acumen and the ability to connect market dynamics, competitive developments, patient or customer trends, and commercial performance with financial outcomes.
• Demonstrated ability to influence decisions and build productive relationships across Commercial, Finance, Marketing, Pricing, Analytics, and Business Insights teams.
• Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate complex analyses clearly to senior management.
• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.
• Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and commitment to data quality and analytical rigor.
• Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and operate as a proactive self-starter.
• Demonstrated agility in prioritizing multiple assignments, navigating ambiguity, and meeting demanding deadlines within a fast-paced, matrixed organization.

• MBA, CPA, or advanced degree preferred.

jobs.title: IT Operations Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT BLACKSMITH

 - We started by building infrastructure to run CI workloads really fast. Our first product helps companies run GitHub Actions substantially faster and cheaper by owning and operating our own global fleet of bare-metal machines rather than renting generic cloud VMs.

 - Today, we orchestrate tens of millions of Firecracker VMs each week, running CI for 10,000+ companies and tens of millions in ARR. We’ve grown 20x so far in 2026.

 - We operate thousands of bare-metal machines across multiple regions, regularly schedule 300k+ vCPUs concurrently, and run a petabyte-scale Ceph cluster that we manage ourselves.

 - We’ve raised $125M from Seed to Series C, led by Sequoia, Google Ventures (GV) & Peak XV Partners, and we’re intentionally building a small, but exceptional team.

 - Blacksmith was founded by a team with deep systems and scaling experience, including building search/ads infrastructure at Faire, and operating large distributed systems at Cockroach Labs. Our GTM is led by Jon Boyer, formerly Head of Sales at Zapier.

 - We're now extending the same CI infrastructure into a broader platform: running agent sandboxes at scale and building our own background coding agent on top of it.


THE ROLE AT BLACKSMITH

We're hiring our first IT Operations Engineer to own the systems and workflows our employees rely on. You'll shape how IT operates at Blacksmith, from onboarding and device management to identity, access and day-to-day support.

This is a hands-on role with broad ownership. You'll solve problems for teammates, automate recurring work, and build processes that scale with the company. You'll also partner with security and engineering to keep our devices, accounts and internal tools secure.


WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Own onboarding, role changes and offboarding end to end, including device procurement, setup and recovery, account provisioning and timely access removal.

 - Resolve employee issues across hardware, software, networking and accounts, and turn recurring problems into reliable, self-service or automated workflows.

 - Operate and improve identity and access management, ensuring employees have the access they need and nothing more.

 - Manage our employee device fleet, including automated enrollment, patching, disk encryption and inventory.

 - Own software administration, licenses and renewals, keeping track of the tools we use and who has access to them.

 - Partner with business teams to build and maintain internal apps and integrations that simplify their work.

 - Partner with security and engineering on endpoint security, access controls and audit readiness, and maintain clear employee guides and operational runbooks.


YOU’RE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - A resourceful approach to troubleshooting and the persistence to work through unfamiliar problems using documentation, investigation and vendor support.

 - A genuine interest in helping people, with the patience and communication skills to support technical and non-technical teammates.

 - A track record of proactively identifying problems and driving them through resolution without waiting for direction, addressing root causes while managing competing priorities.

 - Hands-on experience administering Okta and Google Workspace, with a solid understanding of SSO, MFA, SCIM provisioning and least-privilege access.

 - Experience managing a macOS fleet with Addigy or another MDM, such as Jamf or Kandji, including automated enrollment through Apple Business Manager.

 - Working knowledge of networking fundamentals, including DNS, DHCP, Wi-Fi and VPN troubleshooting.

 - Experience running employee onboarding, offboarding and IT support in a growing organization.

 - The ability to automate repetitive work through scripting, APIs or workflow tools.

 - Strong comfort using coding agents to develop and debug internal tools, integrations and automation, while reviewing changes and validating results.


BONUS

 - You've built or scaled an IT function, or led migrations, tool rollouts or process redesigns in a growing organization.

 - You've supported security or compliance work, such as SOC 2, endpoint security or incident response.

 - You've managed identity or other IT systems through infrastructure as code.

 - You've built internal applications or tools for business teams, translating their needs into practical, maintainable solutions.


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

 - Medical, Vision, and Dental insurance.

 - Competitive base + equity.

 - 401K match.

 - Unlimited PTO.

 - Annual offsite.

 - Early-exercise stock options.

 - 12 weeks fully paid parental leave (US).
