jobs.title: Partner Sales Manager, Systems Integrators
jobs.description:
About Upsun

Upsun is the software factory for human-AI workflows. We give teams one unified platform to create, review, deploy, and run software, with AI agents and humans working in sync. Developers, DevOps engineers, and platform teams use Upsun to build and ship with confidence, without wrestling with infrastructure.

Upsun brings this together through two products: one that shapes the work, and one that runs it.

• Upsun Dispatch™: the AI-first product accelerator. Dispatch governs and simplifies collaboration between AI agents and cross-functional human teams, so work gets shaped, reviewed, and moved to production faster. Ship better code, not just more code.

• Upsun Cloud: the Cloud Application Platform for AI acceleration. Cloud is where that software runs. It helps organizations launch agentic software into production confidently and reliably, with: Predictable performance, even at scale Secure, compliant environments by default Real-time observability and profiling built in Cloning, configuration, and provisioning in seconds Sandbox environments where AI agents can build and test safely

The name says it all. "Up" means uptime, reliability, and acceleration. "Sun" reflects our follow-the-sun-support, a 24x7, globally distributed support team keeping the lights on while you rest. Our core belief is that software should power brighter solutions and greater innovation.

What's our commonality, our cultural fabric? A curious spirit and a thirst for knowledge; an eagerness for innovative ideas and cultures. We believe we can build anything together in an environment that frees you to do your best work.

Our values:

🌿 We make a positive impact.

✨ We aim for the stars.

💚 We care for each other.

Impact of a Partner Sales Manager, Systems Integrators

As Partner Sales Manager, Systems Integrators, you’ll build and grow Upsun’s business with systems integrators and larger digital agencies across North America. This is a quota-carrying role, and a rare chance to shape a new category and go-to-market from the start.

You’ll focus on partners that fit our Ideal Partner Profile (IPP): established technical teams that already run software factories to deliver custom applications for their clients. You’ll sell to CTOs, lead developers, and software architects.

What to expect

• Build the pipeline: Use our IPP to identify, qualify, and prioritize SIs and larger agencies across North America, from existing Upsun partners to net-new logos.

• Own the full sales cycle: Pitch, run discovery, scope pilots, and close deals, from the first conversation with a CTO to signature with procurement and finance.

• Forecast with discipline: Keep Salesforce accurate and report on pipeline, wins, and partner health.

• Turn pilots into practices: Help partners move from a first project to a repeatable delivery practice they sell to their own clients, with Solutions Engineering and Product.

• Grow the whole account: Work closely with our Agency Partner Managers on opportunities, renewals, and expansions at the same partners

• Be the partner’s voice: Bring field feedback from SIs and agencies back to Product to shape our roadmap and partner programs.

• Meet your partners face to face: Visit partners, run roadshows, and represent Upsun at regional events to deepen relationships and grow our visibility in the SI and agency ecosystem.

What you bring

• Partner and new-business experience: 5+ years selling to or through system integrators, consultancies or digital agencies at a SaaS, cloud or developer-tools company, with new-business targets met.

• Technical credibility: You understand how SIs and agencies build and run custom applications (Git, CI/CD, environments, modern frameworks, cloud platforms) and how AI-generated code is reshaping the SDLC. You learn new tech fast and can hold your own with technical stakeholders.

• Value-based selling: You can explain our full value case in the customer’s language and lead with what matters most to the person in front of you, from CTO to CFO. You’re comfortable with pricing, commitments, and contracts, and you can handle the procurement and finance conversation that follows.

• Pilot-to-production mindset: You scope pilots with clear success criteria and turn them into committed, recurring programs.

• Partner-first approach: You build long-term trust with partner executives, practice leads and tech leads, and put partner success at the heart of every deal.

• Ownership and collaboration. You run your territory like your own business, spot opportunity before it shows in the numbers, and act without being asked. You work closely with the Agency team, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Marketing to get partners the right answers fast.

Where we hire

At Upsun, remote work isn’t just a trend. It’s our foundation. Upsunners are a global workforce, and we thrive in a multicultural team. We’re committed to open source and an open, welcoming environment. Our team spans more than 30 countries and a wide range of experience levels, and we’re currently hiring for this role in Canada or the United States. We’re unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time, but we welcome applications from all qualified candidates who are legally authorized to work in these countries.

How we hire

Our interview process is a chance for us to understand how you think, what you’ve built, and what you want to take on next, and for you to get to know us. Together, we’ll explore where your strengths and interests meet the challenges our teams are solving.

We know a great hire won’t meet every requirement above. If you can see yourself making the team better, we want to hear your story. Few of us would be here if someone hadn’t taken a chance on us.

You can expect 4 video interviews interviews on Google Meet to follow the order below.

• 45 Minutes with Talent Acquisition

• 60 Minutes with Hiring Manager (GM, Global Alliance)

• 60 Minutes with team (Strategic Sales Lead)

• 60 Minutes with team (Senior Director, Customer Solutions)

• 45 Minutes with Executive (CRO)

All roles require background checks.

What we offer

💡 A product you can believe in - Join us in transforming how businesses build and manage web applications, driven making a positive impact as a proud B Corp.

🏆 An Award-Winning Workplace - We’ve been recognized by Forbes’ Top 30 Companies for Remote Jobs and France’s Best Workplaces for Women.

🗣️ A culture that values your voice - Join a flexible, open, and inclusive work environment where your voice is encouraged, and your ideas shape our growth and evolution.

🌎 A global team - Collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds across the world, embracing different perspectives

🎉 Benefits and perks - Make the most of what matters to you

🏝 Flexible PTO

🩺 Comprehensive healthcare coverage (UK, Canada, France, Spain, USA)

📈 Company stock options

🧠 Professional development budget

💻 Office equipment budget

💆‍♀️ Wellness budget

🧳 Annual team gatherings

👶 Inclusive parental leave

✈️ Remote work travel program

You belong here

At Upsun, we celebrate diversity in all its forms and are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and supportive workplace where everyone can thrive. We embrace and value different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences, because they make us stronger as a team. Whoever you are, wherever you're from, and whatever path you've taken, you are welcome here. We encourage you to bring your whole self to work, connect with others, and share your passion. If you need accommodations at any stage of our hiring process, please let us know. We're here to ensure an accessible and comfortable experience for you.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer (Palantir Foundry)
jobs.description:
Your Dream. Our Team.

About Rise8

Rise8 builds custom, secure software for government organizations, measuring success by impact: lives saved, time returned, and missions advanced.

We think big, start small, and scale fast with elite teams across product, design, and engineering to drive continuous delivery for critical missions.

We believe customer experience starts with employee experience, so we take care of our employees. Rise8 is where you’ll do the best work of your career—supported by a culture you won’t find anywhere else. We offer competitive pay and benefits, but what sets us apart is our commitment to autonomy, growth, and a culture rooted in kindness, candor, and continuous learning.

Certified as a Great Place to Work®, with 100% of employees saying they love working here, Rise8 is where bold ideas become real capabilities. Where mission meets meaning. And where fewer bad things happen because of bad software.

About You

• You’re mission-driven and measure success by impact (lives saved, time returned, missions advanced), not activity.

• You think big, start small, and scale fast. You treat time as the biggest vulnerability and security as something that enables speed.

• You lead with kindness and candor: you give honest feedback, take it well, and raise the bar for everyone around you.

• You’re an owner. You thrive with autonomy, act decisively, and stay steady when things are uncertain.

• You're building with AI and see it as a force multiplier not a shortcut.

As a Senior Software Engineer at Rise8, you will:

• Work with clients who may be new to modern software practices such as design thinking, AI-assisted and agentic engineering, continuous-release deployment, backlog management, or even interacting directly with the users they provide software to.

• Decompose business problems into clear, actionable instructions and specifications for agentic development.

• Be responsible for learning how your client likes to learn, how they like to receive feedback, and what ubiquitous language they use so you can speak in terms that resonate with them.

• Learn, teach, and refine your approach constantly to best collaborate towards a new way of thinking about engineering.

• On enablement engagements, pair with client developers, engineers, and military service members. Accelerate how they develop and deliver user stories that provide business value, technical feasibility, and user-driven functionality.

• Ensure that development is delivered week over week and continuously gauge feedback from real users in real time.

• Work with a balanced team in mind while building software that fits the user needs, business objectives, and stakeholder vision so the team can quickly make informed engineering decisions based on validated assumptions.

• Plan for and build delivery and user metrics into the software systems you create, so the team can measure real outcomes.

• Lead within your Rise8 product team by tracking and managing tech debt, facilitating engineering discussions, and leveling up less experienced engineers.

Qualifications

• Must have an active DoD security clearance.

• Must have working proficiency to advanced Palantir Foundry / Warp Core experience

• 6-10 years of Software Development experience in a variety of programming languages.

• Strong communication skills and interest in a pair-programming environment.

• Experience leveraging AI in software development.

• Experience with Test Driven Development (TDD) and agile methodologies, including using AI tools to write and maintain tests.

• You have a strong understanding of algorithms, programming language theory, software architecture, networks, databases, and design patterns, and understand how to apply them.

• Experience with both frontend and backend.

• Experience using container technologies such as Docker or Kubernetes.

• Familiarity with DevSecOps tools and processes such as Git, Ansible, GitLabCI, SonarQube, Fortify, and ThreadFix.

• Demonstrated experience with API Development.

• You are comfortable running your software in Linux environments.

• You have strong facilitation skills.

• BA/BS in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience in training, mentoring and/or up-skilling engineers.

• Experience developing cloud-native applications.

• Experience leading a product or development team.

• Experience building and deploying in a continuous delivery environment.

• Experience working directly with clients.

• Experience with DoD, especially at a DoD "Software Factory".

• Preferred, not a requirement: located within a commutable distance into Colorado Springs, CO or El Segundo, CA

Travel

Position may require up to 25% travel in support of contract performance, customer site visits, and program activities.

Salary

The annual salary range for this role as it is posted is $143,824 to $179,780 regardless of final candidate location within the United States. The final job level and annual salary will be determined based on the education, qualification, knowledge, skills, ability, and experience of the final candidate(s), and calibrated against relevant market data and internal team equity.

Benefits

• Flexible schedule in a 100% distributed workforce

• Premium Insurance: We cover up to 100% of the employee premium and up to 80% of the combined dependent premium on our base health plan depending on pay band. We also cover 100% of the premium for employee and dependent Dental and Vision as well as employee premiums for Life and Disability coverage.

• Retirement: 401k match at 10% gross pay.

• Paid time off (PTO): 4 weeks combined accrued vacation and sick leave, 11 Federal holidays, your birthday, jury duty, and bereavement.

• Education & Training: Accrued budget of up to $4,000 per year for classes, travel, events, and materials.

• Wellness Budget: To encourage and support a well-rounded healthy lifestyle, we cover 50% reimbursement on a variety of wellness activities and products, up to $500 per calendar year.

• Equipment: We offer a MacBook Pro and multi-port adapter.

All of Rise8’s work in this area is with Federal Government customers that require our employees involved with their projects be U.S. citizens. As such, this role requires U.S. citizenship. If hired, you would also be required to go through a background investigation.

Rise8 is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer that will consider you for this role regardless of race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, marital status, gender identity or expression, national origin, genetics, age, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Reporting Clinical Laboratory Scientist (contractor)
jobs.description:
A Rare Opportunity to Shape the Future of Genomics

Join a team of brilliant, passionate innovators determined to transform healthcare. At BillionToOne, we've built a category-defining, publicly traded company on Nasdaq where transparency fuels trust, collaboration drives breakthroughs, and every contribution moves the needle on our mission to make life-changing diagnostics accessible to all. We don't just aim for incremental improvements; we build products that are 10x better than anything that exists today.

Our scientists, engineers, sales executives, and visionaries are united by an unwavering commitment to changing the standard of care in prenatal and cancer diagnostics. This is where cutting-edge science meets human compassion, and every innovation you contribute helps remove the fear of the unknown from some of life's most critical medical moments.

If you're driven by purpose, energized by innovation, and ready to help shape the future of precision medicine at scale, this is where you belong.

The Prenatal Reporting Clinical Laboratory Scientist (RCLS) contractor is responsible for performing high-complexity clinical laboratory data analysis, reviewing and interpreting molecular diagnostic and sequencing results, and ensuring the accuracy, reliability, and timely reporting of patient results in accordance with established laboratory procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.

The RCLS independently executes validated bioinformatics pipelines, evaluates analytical results and quality control metrics, troubleshoots, and reviews and releases clinical laboratory reports within established authorization and reporting procedures. For complex or unusual results requiring additional evaluation, the RCLS collaborates with Bioinformatics, the Laboratory Directors, and other appropriate clinical personnel to ensure accurate interpretation and reporting.

In addition to routine clinical reporting responsibilities, the RCLS is expected to demonstrate technical leadership by exercising sound scientific judgment, independently investigating complex analytical issues, providing technical guidance to colleagues, supporting personnel training, and identifying opportunities for continuous process improvement. The RCLS may also participate in additional technical leadership activities and cross-functional initiatives as assigned by laboratory leadership.

The RCLS collaborates closely with Laboratory Operations, Bioinformatics, Quality Assurance Management, Genetic Counselors, the Laboratory Directors and other cross-functional teams to support accurate clinical reporting, resolve technical challenges, and maintain efficient laboratory workflows.

The nature of this position requires exceptional attention to detail, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced clinical laboratory environment. The successful candidate must demonstrate initiative, accountability, adaptability, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively. This role is a hybrid work arrangement requiring approximately 60% on-site presence at the Union City and/or Menlo Park offices (three days per week on-site and two days per week remote).

Responsibilities:

Analysis and Reporting (70%)
Clinical Genomic Data Analysis and Interpretation

• Execute established and validated bioinformatics pipelines to process and analyze molecular diagnostic data from patient samples.

• Independently review and interpret clinical genomic data, including sequencing results, bioinformatics outputs, and associated quality control metrics, to ensure results meet established quality standards and reporting criteria.

• Identify, investigate, and troubleshoot analytical discrepancies, unusual findings, and potential data quality issues, collaborating with Bioinformatics and other appropriate technical teams to resolve complex issues as needed.

• Independently manage daily sample analysis priorities, monitor analytical workflows, and proactively communicate technical issues or concerns that may impact reporting accuracy or turnaround times.

Clinical Reporting and Quality Review

• Independently review, verify, and release clinical laboratory reports in accordance with established procedures, documented personnel authorization, and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Collaborate with other RCLSs, Bioinformatics, Genetic Counselors, Laboratory Directors, and other appropriate clinical personnel to evaluate complex findings, resolve reporting discrepancies, and obtain additional review or approval when necessary.

• Ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of clinical reports while managing daily reporting priorities and maintaining established quality standards and turnaround time expectations.

• Maintain accurate documentation of analytical reviews, quality assessments, investigations, and reporting decisions in accordance with established laboratory procedures.

• Communicate reporting concerns and unresolved issues promptly to appropriate personnel, supporting continuity of reporting operations and timely resolution of sample-specific issues.

Technical Leadership, Quality Assurance, and Operational Support (30%)
Technical Leadership and Training

• Demonstrate initiative, accountability, and sound scientific judgment when performing clinical data analysis and reporting responsibilities.

• Independently investigate complex analytical discrepancies, troubleshoot technical issues, and identify appropriate solutions or escalation pathways.

• Serve as a technical resource for other Reporting CLS personnel by sharing knowledge, providing guidance, and supporting consistent application of established analytical and reporting procedures.

• Assist with training, onboarding, and mentoring Reporting CLS personnel and other clinical laboratory staff as appropriate.

• Promote technical competency, reporting consistency, and adherence to established laboratory procedures and quality standards.

• Proactively identify opportunities to improve reporting accuracy, workflow efficiency, and overall laboratory performance.

• Participate in additional technical leadership activities, such as coordinating technical investigations, supporting validation projects, or contributing to workflow improvements, as assigned by laboratory leadership.

Quality Assurance and Regulatory Compliance

• Perform and support quality control and quality assurance activities to maintain the accuracy, reliability, and integrity of clinical laboratory testing and reporting.

• Ensure compliance with applicable Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), College of American Pathologists (CAP), California state regulations, and established laboratory policies and procedures.

• Identify, document, and investigate quality-related issues, including analytical discrepancies, nonconforming results, and deviations from established procedures.

• Collaborate with Quality Management and laboratory leadership to support root cause investigations, corrective and preventive actions, and continuous quality improvement initiatives.

• Maintain accurate documentation and records in accordance with established quality management and regulatory requirements.

Process Improvement and Workflow Optimization

• Identify and recommend opportunities to optimize analytical workflows, improve reporting accuracy, enhance operational efficiency, and promote cost-effective laboratory practices.

• Collaborate with Laboratory Operations, Bioinformatics, Genetic Counselors, and Process Engineering teams to support the development, validation, implementation, and optimization of new or updated laboratory tests, analytical methodologies, and reporting workflows.

• Assist with technology transfer and implementation of validated methodologies from Process Engineering into the clinical laboratory.

• Support the evaluation and implementation of improvements to laboratory data management and reporting systems.

• Maintain and update reporting procedures, technical documentation, and workflow resources to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compatibility with established laboratory processes.

• Participate in investigations of recurring analytical or workflow issues and contribute to the development and implementation of appropriate solutions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Operational Support

• Collaborate with Laboratory Operations, Bioinformatics, Genetic Counseling, Client Services, Quality Assurance Management, and Process Engineering to investigate and resolve sample-specific and workflow-related issues.

• Communicate analytical findings, technical concerns, and recommended solutions clearly and effectively to relevant stakeholders.

• Serve as a technical point of contact for cross-functional teams when addressing clinical reporting questions or troubleshooting analytical issues, as appropriate.

• Support laboratory leadership with reporting priorities, operational coordination, and project deliverables as needed.

• Contribute to cross-functional initiatives that improve laboratory efficiency, reporting reliability, and overall operational performance.

Qualifications:

• Must possess an active and valid CLS or Clinical Genetic Molecular Biologist Scientist (CGMBS) license issued by the state of California pursuant to Division 2, Chapter 3 of the California Business and Professions Code or to practice medicine, osteopathy or podiatry pursuant to Division 2, Chapter 5 of the California Business and Professions Code appropriate to the specialty they are performing

• Bachelor's degree or higher in Biomedical Laboratory Sciences, Clinical Laboratory Science, Molecular Biology, Genetics, or a related scientific discipline, consistent with applicable licensure requirements.

• At least one year of clinical laboratory experience or equivalent experience in a high-complexity, high-volume molecular diagnostic clinical laboratory environment.

• Working knowledge of molecular biology principles, clinical laboratory testing methodologies, and applicable local, state, and federal laboratory regulations.

• Demonstrated experience with sequencing data analysis, including evaluation and interpretation of next-generation sequencing (NGS) results and associated analytical quality control metrics in accordance with validated laboratory procedures.

• Demonstrated ability to independently analyze complex laboratory data, investigate discrepancies, and troubleshoot issues affecting test performance or reporting accuracy.

• Familiarity with bioinformatics analysis outputs and their application to clinical molecular diagnostic reporting.

• Strong computer skills and the ability to effectively use laboratory data management systems and analytical software. Proficiency with commonly used workplace and collaboration tools, including Atlassian Suite, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Office Suite.

• Strong analytical judgment, attention to detail, and organizational and problem-solving skills, with a commitment to accurate and reliable clinical reporting.

• Ability to independently manage reporting responsibilities, prioritize competing demands, and adapt to changing operational needs while maintaining quality and turnaround time expectations.

• Demonstrated initiative and accountability in investigating technical issues, identifying solutions, and exercising appropriate judgment regarding consultation and escalation.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to provide technical guidance and collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams.

• Receptiveness to feedback and commitment to continuous learning, professional development, and process improvement.

Benefits And Perks:

• Working alongside brilliant, kind, passionate and dedicated colleagues, in an empowering environment, toward a global vision, striving for a future in which transformative molecular diagnostics can help millions of patients

• The ability to indirectly or directly change the lives of hundreds of thousands patients

• Daily on-site lunches provided from top eateries

• A variety of perks on campus (state of the art gym, restaurant)

• Free on-site EV charging (compatible with all EVs, including Tesla)

For this position, the target hourly rate is: $65 per hour.

BillionToOne is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

For more information about how we protect your information, we encourage you to review our Privacy Policy.

BillionToOne is a next-generation molecular diagnostics company on a mission to make powerful, accurate diagnostic tests accessible to everyone. Our revolutionary QCT molecular counting technology enhances disease detection resolution by over a thousandfold using cell-free DNA,a breakthrough that has already transformed the lives of over half a million patients worldwide.

Our Impact

Unity Complete™ is the only non-invasive prenatal screen capable of assessing fetal risk for both common recessive conditions and aneuploidies from a single maternal blood sample.
Unity Confirm™ enables non-invasive confirmation for high-risk screening results through the capture of intact circulating fetal cells using BillionToOne’s Fetal Cell Capture™ Technology.
Our Northstar® liquid biopsy test uniquely combines treatment selection with real-time monitoring, giving oncologists unprecedented precision in cancer care.

Our Growth

From $0 to $400M+ annualized revenue run-rate in just 6 years. In 2025, we completed one of the most successful IPOs for a medical diagnostics company, building on nearly $400M in private funding,including our $130M Series D in 2024 and backed by world-class investors including Hummingbird, Adams Street Partners, Neuberger Berman, Baillie Gifford, and Premji Invest.

Our Recognition

Forbes named us one of America's Best Startup Employers for 2025 and we're Great Place to Work certified, with 100% of our people willing to go the extra mile, even as we've scaled to over 700 employees.

Our Future

Headquartered in Menlo Park with facilities in Union City, CA, and a new lab opening in Austin, TX in 2027, we're continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible in molecular diagnostics. We're just getting started.

Ready to help us change the world, one molecule at a time? Learn more at billiontoone.com

jobs.title: Producer
jobs.description:
NBC News is seeking a seasoned, driven Producer to support newsgathering, storytelling, and live production across all platforms. This role will work closely with a Correspondent and production teams to pitch, develop, report, and execute compelling journalism—from breaking news to in-depth features, investigative reporting to national coverage.

The ideal candidate is a creative journalist with sharp editorial judgment, strong writing and research skills, and the confidence to thrive under pressure. This producer should be equally at home in the field, on location, or in the control room, and adept at delivering both live and taped segments that meet NBC’s highest editorial standards. The ideal candidate is a news junkie who can’t wait to get out the door and, on the road, to cover that next story. This producer should also enjoy storytelling for morning television, an evening newscast and everything in between. The ability to shoot and edit is a plus, along with a sense of what does well on social media or in vertical video formats.

This role is right for you if you’re a versatile storyteller who thrives on urgency and impact. You move seamlessly between producing, reporting, and writing, and you’re as comfortable leading coverage during breaking news as you are crafting enterprise stories. You’re highly organized, competitive, and relentless about accuracy and detail—yet collaborative, adaptable, and energized by working with correspondents and teams under tight deadlines. Most importantly, you’re passionate about journalism that informs, engages, and makes a difference.

Responsibilities:

• Partner with Correspondent and show teams to develop, report, and deliver strong, visually compelling stories with clear narratives and well-researched journalism.
• Pitch, field produce, write, and fact-check stories across NBC News linear and streaming platforms, including daily news, longform pieces, and cross-platform content.
• Conduct original reporting, deep research, and source interviews.
• Secure guest bookings in a competitive environment; conduct pre-interviews and prepare talking points.
• Ability to travel at a moment’s notice to cover a story and commit to staying on the road as long as the story takes.
• Collaborate with control rooms, senior producers, and editorial teams to build rundowns, write intros, and produce live and taped segments.
• Oversee field operations, including live shots, remote anchor setups, and breaking news coverage.
• Track and manage correspondent’s schedule when working with them closely.
• Work closely with editors to ensure high-quality video packages, graphics, and sound.
• Partner with Standards & Legal to ensure all content adheres to editorial and corporate guidelines.
• Maintain strong communication between the Correspondent, senior leadership, assignment desk and production teams.
• Contribute ideas for a wide range of content including news-of-day, lifestyle features, celebrity interviews, and human-interest stories.

Basic Requirements:

• Bachelor’s degree in journalism, communications, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
• Minimum 5 years’ experience in network news, cable, or talk show production, including live and taped segments.
• Strong journalistic writing, research, and editorial judgment skills.
• Demonstrated knowledge of U.S. politics, current events, pop culture, and lifestyle trends.
• Experience shooting (DSLR or iPhone) and editing (Avid and/or Adobe Premiere).
• Strong ability to navigate newsroom tools and technology (Slack, NCX, Latakoo, etc.)
• Proven ability to work in fast-paced environments under tight deadlines.
• Must be willing to work nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime with short notice.
• Must be able to travel frequently, domestically and internationally.
• Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
• Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills; ability to collaborate across teams.

Desired Characteristics:

• Strong storytelling ability with creativity in pitching original ideas.
• Experience working with live programming.
• Cool under pressure and comfortable managing breaking news situations.
• A self-starter with strong organizational and multitasking skills.
• Knowledge of NBC News Policies, Guidelines, and Practices.

Additional Requirements:

Fully Remote: This position has been designated as fully remote, based in Dallas, TX, meaning that the position is expected to contribute from a non-NBCUniversal worksite, most commonly an employee’s residence. This role will report to Miami bureau leadership.

This position is eligible for company-sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: 95,000 - 135,000

As part of our selection process, external candidates may be required to attend an in-person interview with an NBCUniversal employee at one of our locations prior to a hiring decision. You can request reasonable accommodations by emailing AccessibilitySupport@nbcuni.com.

jobs.title: Retail Floor Lead-Easton
jobs.description:
The role of Retail Store Floor Lead at Vuori is to lead the retail sales team by example, forging connections with customers while communicating Vuori’s brand values through insightful product knowledge and a happy, optimistic outlook. Also, encouraging the team on how to maintain Vuori’s standards in retail sales and customer experiences. The Floor Lead is a key part of the store leadership team and as such supervises the retail floor and takes initiative, delegates work and is a “go to” person. Under the direction of the Store Manager, the floor lead position assists in any leadership duties that arise, thereby working directly with both the Store Manager and Assistant Store Manager.

What you'll get to do:

Create an unforgettable customer experience

• Works with the sales team to ensure each customer receives the best experience possible.
• Takes ownership of the sales floor and sales team to ensure customer experience is the first priority.
• Prepare the fitting rooms, find sizes, and provide honest knowledgeable feedback to customers regarding merchandise style and fit.
• Forge lasting relationships with customers by engaging with them about product details, new product and replenishment and invite them to upcoming events.
• Be knowledgeable on what’s new and what’s selling well and shares with both the customer and team.

Be the business

• Leads the team on the day to day operations of the store when the Store Manager or Assistant Store Manager is not in.
• Motivates the sales team and achieves sales goals in a team-based commission environment.
• Seek new product knowledge in the broader fashion landscape and active-wear specifically to serve as an expert for the customer.
• Leads the team in the completion of projects while keeping the focus on customer experience.

jobs.title: Process Development Engineer, Additive Manufacturing
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



Within Additive Manufacturing, you'll be the go to technical resource for process development, owning how we build, iterate, and automate the way we develop and mature our additive processes across various types of additive manufacturing. We're not approaching this the way additive has traditionally been done. We're rethinking it from the ground up, using automation, AI, and new software tools to move past the constraints that have limited additive. You'll be the process expert tying materials, process, and in process monitoring together, delivering the kind of innovative approach that lets us move quickly and work past the time constraints that have historically slowed this work down. This role is for someone ready to be challenged and take on highly technical work with the resources to push for innovation in additive manufacturing, helping build and refine the tools and processes that make our additive capabilities faster and more scalable over time.


The Role

 - Lead process and parameter development for additive processes, with a primary focus on metals. Executing DOEs to define and measure process windows and drive machine, material, and process readiness.

 - Drive adoption of in situ monitoring, statistical process control, and digital traceability records.

 - Build software tools internally, or evaluate and implement existing tools on the market, to accelerate parameter development and process automation.

 - Continuously research, evaluate, and bring in novel tools and technologies that support and strengthen process development capability.

 - Design and build automated workflows and creative methods to efficiently validate and implement.

 - Serve as the point of contact for developing specific parameter needs tied to unique part geometries or to overcome platform specific challenges.

 - Work closely with the materials engineering team to roll out, validate, and implement new parameters and processes into production.

 - Work cross functionally with applications engineers, materials engineers, systems engineers, software engineering, and welding engineers.



What We're Looking For

 - Master's degree in an engineering discipline.

 - 3+ years of experience developing and optimizing parameters and processes for additive manufacturing, with a strong focus on metal processes.

 - Hands on experience with additive manufacturing equipment and software, including build processors or process simulation tools.

 - Experience building or improving automated workflows, scripting, or tooling to speed up process or parameter development.

 - Ability to work closely with materials engineering to translate new materials into validated, production ready processes.

 - Comfort working in an undefined space, building new processes and tools rather than relying on established norms.

 - U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident (required for ITAR compliance).
   
   

What Will Set You Apart

 - Extensive experience in LPBF as the primary process, with DED experience as a secondary strength.

 - Background in aerospace, aviation, defense, energy, or similar industries with high specification requirements.

 - Experience with in situ process monitoring and using that data to inform parameter development.

 - Programming or scripting experience, such as Python, used to automate engineering workflows.

 - Familiarity with industry specialized material standards, certification requirements, or quality systems such as NADCAP, AMS7000 series, AS9100, and relevant ASTM/AMS additive manufacturing specifications.

 - Familiarity with fracture control classification of components and associated qualification requirements.

 - Prior support of production scale up in high-rate manufacturing environments.
   

Compensation:

For this role, the target salary range is $135,000 - $200,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.



BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

 


USE OF AI IN HIRING

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy https://www.hadrian.co/privacy-policy.

 


CONSIDERATION OF CRIMINAL HISTORY

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

 


HADRIAN IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

jobs.title: Senior National Account Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT GOODR

We create and sell active eyewear for anyone. No Slip. No Bounce. All Polarized. All Fun. Interested in joining our team? Keep reading.

OUR VALUES: We have two core values: Fun & Authenticity.

• FUN = Being sh*tty isn’t fun. Agreed? Taking pride in your work, finding joy in being GREAT, and celebrating wins… and losses. Now, that’s fun!

• AUTHENTICITY = Focusing on being authentic over being liked. (Next-level guru stuff. Count it.)

Fun Fact: We do not allow email to be sent internally. Carrier pigeons only. JK, we use Slack.

AUTONOMY: We practice autonomy, empowerment, and accountability so that every team member can be in control of their own life.

• HYBRID WORKING: This role is required to be in the Inglewood office every Tuesday and Thursday with the occasional third day thrown in.

• PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT: We have an all-company learning program so that we’re constantly leveling up our skills.

SUSTAINABILITY: We think Earth’s pretty rad. That’s why we take action wherever possible to limit our impact on the planet.

• 1% FOR THE PLANET MEMBER: 1% of goodr’s annual sales go directly to environmental organizations.

• CARBON NEUTRAL: In 2019, goodr became a 100% carbon neutral company.

Fun Fact: goodr celebrates every Earth Day by releasing limited-edition sunglasses with frames made from 100% recycled materials—and the packaging is 100% sustainable, too!

ABOUT THE ROLE

We know why you’re here. It’s because back in middle school, you didn't just run the bake sale—you single-handedly negotiated end-cap shelf space with the principal, convinced the local grocery store to donate supplies, and turned a $50 budget into a massive multi-thousand-dollar fundraising empire. You didn’t just sell cookies; you owned the distribution network.

That rare mix of big-picture strategy, ruthless retail charm, and absolute operational mastery makes you the ultimate retail mastermind we need to tackle the absolute big dogs: Target and Dick’s Sporting Goods (DSG). In this role, you’ll act as both the strategic visionary and the high-energy account owner, making sure our sunglasses dominate the shelves, our inventory moves like wildfire, and our retail partners view us as their absolute favorite, can't-live-without brand. So channel that powerhouse retail energy and apply today to be goodr’s Senior National Account Manager!

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Own the overall strategic vision, revenue, and profit targets for two of our biggest accounts: our Target and Dick’s Sporting Goods (DSG)

• Lead Joint Business Planning (JBP) and craft multi-year growth strategies that expand distribution, doors, and product performance

• Build and nurture rock-solid relationships with buyers, merchants, and senior decision-makers across both account empires

• Work with our retail agency to align on media strategies and investments with account priorities, promotional plans, and sales objectives to drive growth and maximize performance.

• Partner with Product, Planning, and Finance to build bulletproof account forecasts, optimize pricing, and curate high-velocity assortments

• Collaborate with Marketing to cook up retailer-specific marketing campaigns, co-promotions, and head-turning in-store moments

• Translate sell-through data and retail math into killer commercial strategies that close forecast gaps before they even happen

• Serve as the ultimate internal connective tissue across Sales, Operations, Supply Chain, and Digital to execute account wins flawlessly

• Deliver high-impact business reviews and product presentations that make Target and DSG wonder how they ever survived without us

• Track and analyze account KPIs, margins, and inventory health to ensure every SKU on every shelf is pulling its weight

• No direct reports – you get to lead the charge/channel/category/strategy, without managing your fellow flamingos

• This role is in the National Sales team and will report directly to the Director of National Sales

• Perform other related duties as assigned

ABOUT THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

• May or may not have a degree...we don’t care (bonus points for Basset Hound Science or Dinosaur Law)

• 6+ years proven working experience managing major national wholesale accounts in CPG, active lifestyle, or retail brands

• Proven track record of directly owning and scaling massive retail partnerships (experience with Target and/or DSG is a major flex)

• Proven ability to negotiate complex contracts and execute joint business plans that drive visible results

• Strong understanding of wholesale sales, retail math, forecasting inventory, assortment planning, and profitability

• Expert cross-functional collaborator who can align Planning, Operations, Marketing, and Finance without direct authority

• Expert presenter who is comfortable commanding a room and sharing the goodr vision with large groups

• Working experience using Salesforce and NetSuite, with the ability to navigate advanced Retail analytics platforms with ease

• Strong working knowledge of Asana is a BIG plus

• Possesses a valid driver's license and the flexibility to travel up to 10% for key meetings and account events

• Wakes up every single day obsessing over how to make our key partners bigger, healthier, and more profitable

• Strong communicator who lives into collaboration and loves giving and getting feedback

• Is proactive and an independent problem solver! (Can you google a question?)

WHAT YOU GET

• A role at a company that is going to the moon

• The opportunity to show up every day and have fun

• The ability to learn and grow as a person

• Paid vacation (we encourage you to take time off!)

• Paycheck... obviously. Salary range: $130k - $145k, final offer will be made within this range based on experience

• Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits

• 401(K) with company matching

• Financial Wellness Counseling

• Sunglasses. Obviously.

**No Visa Sponsorship is available for this position.

NEXT STEPS

Here's what we expect the hiring process for this role to be, should all go well with your candidacy. This entire process is expected to take 8 weeks to complete and you'd be expected to start on a specific date.

1. Application

2. Fill out a form with basic questions

3. 30 minute introductory interview with HR team member

4. 30 minute virtual interviews with peers and manager

5. Final assignment and presentation

6. Offer!

TO GET THE PROCESS STARTED, REVIEW & SUBMIT THE FOLLOWING:

• Review goodr's Applicant Privacy Policy. By submitting an application to goodr, you are confirming that you have read the Applicant Privacy Policy and agree to its terms. (Because nothing says “fun” like reading legal documents!)

goodr is committed to providing an accessible and inclusive hiring process. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application, interview, or hiring process, please contact us at accommodations@goodr.com so we can discuss appropriate accommodations.

jobs.title: Instrumentation & Controls Technician (Power Plant) - Memphis
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

INSTRUMENTATION & CONTROLS TECHNICIAN (POWER GENERATION)

As an Instrumentation & Controls Technician, you will keep the controls and field instruments reliable on SpaceXAI’s on-site power plant. The plant supplies power for high-density AI supercomputing facilities in the Memphis and Southaven area, and it has to stay online 24/7.

You will calibrate, troubleshoot, and repair the instruments and control systems on gas turbines and generators, balance-of-plant, fuel gas and process/fluid systems, water, compressed and instrument air, HVAC, and cooling. The turbine fleet is several different manufacturers, and the control platforms are not the same. You are expected to be proficient on every type on site, not specialized in one OEM. Your schedule flexes, including nights, weekends, holidays, and callouts, so the plant always has I&C coverage. This is a full-time, on-site role in the Memphis region.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Calibrate, test, troubleshoot, and repair field instruments and final elements, including transmitters, switches, analyzers, thermocouples, RTDs, control valves, and actuators

• Troubleshoot turbine, generator, and balance-of-plant control systems across every manufacturer on site, including PLCs, turbine controls, and the plant control system

• Find and fix trips, alarms, and bad instrument readings with the shift team and return equipment to service

• Run loop checks and functional checks during start-up, shutdown, commissioning, and outages

• Read and work from P&IDs, loop sheets, wiring diagrams, cause-and-effect charts, and control logic

• Complete calibrations and repairs to procedure, and record as-found/as-left results and work-order closeout in the CMMS

• Identify repeat instrument and controls failures and correct the cause, not only the symptom

• Use AI tools to troubleshoot faster and to simplify calibration records, procedures, and shift handoffs

• Follow SpaceXSI safety procedures, including LOTO, NFPA 70E / arc-flash, confined space, and hot work. Stop work when conditions are unsafe

• Flex shifts and work hours, including nights, weekends, holidays, and callouts, to maintain 24/7 I&C coverage

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate.

• 3+ years of hands-on instrumentation and controls maintenance in a power plant, generating station, or other high-reliability industrial facility.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience with gas turbine or generator controls from more than one manufacturer

• Experience with PLCs, turbine control systems, and a plant DCS or equivalent control system

• Experience calibrating and troubleshooting 4–20 mA loops, HART devices, control valves, and instrument air

• Experience with fuel-gas, water, or balance-of-plant process instruments

• Ability to read P&IDs, loop sheets, electrical schematics, and control logic

• Experience with LOTO and NFPA 70E / arc-flash practices when working in control panels

• Experience using a CMMS, including calibration records and work-order closeout

• Experience supporting commissioning, outages, or trip investigations

• Associate’s degree or technical certificate in instrumentation, controls, or a related field

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Willingness to perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights

• Remain focused while working in hazardous environments, while wearing appropriate PPE

• Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs unassisted

• Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position

• Must be able to work on-site at the power generation facility, with potential travel to other SpaceXSI sites

• Valid driver’s license

SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Electrical Safety Engineer
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

ELECTRICAL SAFETY ENGINEER

The Environmental Health and Safety Business Operations team is seeking a highly driven electrical safety engineer to support how EHS runs electrical safety across SpaceX production, test, and launch infrastructure. This role builds and maintains the programs, procedures, training, metrics, and compliance processes the team uses to keep medium- and low-voltage power systems, manufacturing equipment, ground support systems, and construction power aligned with personnel-protection and control-reliability requirements as operations scale. The ideal candidate will have a comprehensive understanding of industrial electrical system architecture, NFPA 70E electrical safety work practices, and the hazards associated with switchgear, motor control centers, transformers, generators, temporary power, and equipment in hazardous locations.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Support the EHS Business Operations team in administering the electrical safety program in accordance with NFPA 70E, including shock protection, arc-flash protection, energized electrical work permits, approach boundaries, and electrically safe work conditions

• Develop, maintain, and control lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, switching-order templates, and live-dead-live verification practices for switchgear, motor control centers, transformers, automatic transfer switches (ATS), generators, distribution equipment, and production and ground-support loads

• Coordinate arc-flash hazard analysis and incident energy studies (IEEE 1584), maintain equipment-labeling standards, and define PPE categories, working distances, and restricted/limited approach boundaries for AC and DC systems, including outdoor installations

• Support qualification, training, and audit of electrical workers as NFPA 70E Qualified Persons; develop electrical safety training content and tracking for operators, technicians, contractors, and construction partners

• Maintain the review and approval process for energized work, electrical switching, and commissioning procedures; define the criteria EHS uses to stop work when conditions do not meet electrically safe work practice requirements

• Maintain standards for grounding, bonding, equipotential bonding, lightning protection, and power quality monitoring so equipment damage and personnel injury are prevented

• Document and maintain generator, ATS, and backup-power transfer expectations for personnel safety during planned and unplanned transfers, including black-start, paralleling, and restoration during utility outages, storms, and site operations

• Partner with design, construction, and commissioning teams on behalf of EHS Business Operations to integrate electrical safety into new builds and expansions: one-line diagrams, protective device coordination, short-circuit studies, temporary power, and construction LOTO across production, test, and launch areas

• Run structured risk assessments of electrical systems, including Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) and electrical hazard assessments for medium- and low-voltage distribution, classified hazardous locations, and high-energy equipment, and feed results into EHS risk and action tracking

• Support investigation of electrical incidents, near misses, shock events, and arc-flash events; track root-cause analysis and corrective actions to closure

• Track and report electrical hazards associated with hot work near energized equipment, cooling or ventilation failures, and environmental conditions that degrade insulation, PPE, enclosures, and equipment ratings

• Maintain safe operating limits and emergency response procedures for electrical events, including arc flash, shock, power loss, and fire involving electrical equipment, aligned with site emergency response and operational constraints

• Maintain compliance processes for applicable codes and standards, including NFPA 70 (NEC) as adopted by the applicable jurisdiction, NFPA 70E, NFPA 70B, OSHA 1910 Subpart S, IEEE, IEC, and hazardous-location requirements

• Coordinate with contractors, vendors, and utility providers so electrical safety requirements are enforced during installation, maintenance, interconnection, and repairs on power infrastructure

• Own electrical safety metrics, audit readiness, document control, and recurring business reviews so EHS leadership can see program health, gaps, and corrective-action status across supported operations

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, electrical and computer engineering, electrical engineering technology, or related engineering field

• 3+ years of professional experience in electrical power systems, electrical safety, or industrial electrical operations

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Direct ownership or administration of an NFPA 70E electrical safety program in an industrial, utility, manufacturing, or other high-hazard environment

• Hands-on experience in manufacturing plants, heavy industrial facilities, utilities, or large construction sites, including outdoor or harsh-environment installations

• Experience with arc-flash studies, short-circuit analysis, and protective device coordination using ETAP, SKM PowerTools, EasyPower, or equivalent

• Working knowledge of industrial electrical architecture, including utility feeds, substations, switchgear, transformers, motor control centers, generators, paralleling equipment, ATS, and temporary construction power

• Familiarity with delta/wye transformers, protective relaying, facility grounding, lightning protection, and power quality

• Experience with NEC hazardous (classified) locations and electrical work near flammable or energetic operations

• Experience creating and implementing electrical LOTO, switching procedures, and energized electrical work permit processes on active construction or operating sites

• Knowledge of OSHA 1910.147, OSHA 1910.269/1910.333, NFPA 70, NFPA 70B, IEEE 1584, and NESC as applicableNFPA 70E related certifications (e.g., CESCP, CESW, or equivalent electrical safety credentials)

• PE (Professional Engineer) license

• CSP (Certified Safety Professional) or equivalent EHS credential

• Proficiency in AutoCAD Electrical, Revit, or similar electrical design tools

• Proficiency with PFMEA, root cause analysis, statistical process control, and structured problem-solving methodologies

• Experience supporting an EHS or operations team with program governance, metrics, audits, training administration, or document control across more than one site

• Experience working with utility providers, electrical contractors, and commissioning agents on interconnection, cutovers, and live-facility work

• Ability to quickly assess an electrical issue and guide technicians through safe troubleshooting and repair

• Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, enthusiasm for the mission of enabling multi-planetary life

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Relocation is required if not already local to a SpaceX site.

• This is not a remote or hybrid position

• Position requires the ability to travel and support critical infrastructure as needed

• Ability to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support construction, commissioning, test, and launch operations

• Must be able to work in industrial environments and comply with site access and safety requirements when on location

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to CFO and CLO

Our AI-enabled platform turns siloed and disconnected data into operational intelligence — instantly surfacing mission-critical information to empower better, faster decisions that improve outcomes at every touchpoint. Today Peregrine supports hundreds of customers across 30+ states and two countries, serving more than 125 million people — and we’re amplifying our impact as we expand into the enterprise and internationally.

The Executive Assistant Role

We are seeking a highly organized, proactive, and experienced Executive Assistant to support our Chief Financial Officer and Chief Legal Officer. This role provides high-touch, hands-on executive support in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. The ideal candidate has prior experience supporting C-suite executives, thrives in a dynamic startup environment, and enjoys the day-to-day responsibilities of being a trusted Executive Assistant.

This role is well suited for someone who is exceptionally organized, resourceful, and adaptable, with the ability to manage complex calendars, coordinate meetings and travel, anticipate executive needs, and navigate shifting priorities with ease. • Build empathetic relationships with ease, maintaining strong situational awareness of team culture and morale while helping executives recognize key milestones and achievements.

• Strong traditional EA skill set, including calendar management, travel coordination, expense reporting, meeting planning, and general administrative support.

jobs.title: Lead DVM- Chicago (South Loop), IL
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a Lead Emergency Veterinarian at VEG, beyond helping people and their pets, you’ll take ownership of supporting your team and ensuring that your hospital is a model of clinical excellence. Working alongside your hospital’s medical director, you’ll champion VEG’s medical processes and initiatives, developing your fellow doctors and coaching them to thrive. You’re well-versed in the VEG Spikes, our unique, customer-centered way of doing things—like ensuring people see a doctor right away and allowing families to stay with their pets—and you lead by example, ensuring your team practices the VEG way with every case. In this role, you’ll find ways to say yes to providing the guidance, resources, and encouragement your team needs to grow confidently in their careers. As a leader, you’ll have the opportunity to foster a culture of mentorship and learning, helping your doctors build fulfilling, unexpected career paths while creating a lasting impact on your hospital.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Work clinical shifts, with responsibilities consistent with emergency doctors at your VEG:

• Answer medical questions over the phone

• See patients right away as part of the VEG Triage and VEG Spikes, our unique, customer-centered way of doing things—like ensuring people see a doctor right away and allowing families to stay with their pets

• Complete a diagnosis of each pet's condition to create a diagnostic and therapeutic plan

• Communicate diagnosis and treatment options directly with customers

• Provide appropriate treatments to address each pet’s specific condition

• Create and review medical records to ensure accuracy

• Demonstrate the value of tests and treatments performed by speaking with the customer and addressing their concerns

• Coach fellow doctors on medical excellence, doctoring the VEG Way, and providing VEG’s customer-focused experience

• Support fellow doctors through their assigned growth and development plans

• Assist Medical Director (MD) when coverage is needed due to callouts or schedule changes

• Work as interim MD when the current MD is on leave or opening a new VEG hospital

• Lead monthly doctor meetings and M&M rounds with guidance from the MD

• Teaching hospitals only: If needed, own the New ER Doctor (NERD) training program and perform all NERD MD job duties.

• Create doctor schedules, including managing leave requests and posting schedules at least two months in advance

• Address customer complaints related to medical concerns.

WHAT YOU NEED

• A DVM, VMD, or equivalent degree

• 2+ years of ER experience and critical case management

• One year leadership experience is preferred, but not required

• Training in emergency surgery/endoscopy

• Flexible to work a combination of clinical and administrative shifts

• Ensure top-tier customer satisfaction and hospital revenue production

• Willingness to lead and support fellow doctors, as well as perform administrative tasks during off hours (i.e. doctor callouts, addressing customer complaints, scheduling)

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation, including base and 401K match

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including QPR training and access to free therapy or counseling

• Based on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave, up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

Location

We're currently considering candidates who are willing to work all their hours from our headquarters in Lincoln, NE alongside their teammates.  Remote work is not an option at this time.

Must-Haves

• A current student. You’re excited for the opportunity to work with our partnerships team because it’ll complement and enhance your education and give you a leg up when you take your next steps after school.

jobs.title: Supervisor, Spaceport Operations (Transportation)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SUPERVISOR, SPACEPORT OPERATIONS (TRANSPORTATION)

The Spaceport Operations Supervisor will develop, manage, market, provide strategic direction, and oversight of transportation programs (employee commute shuttles, on-site shuttles, airport shuttles, Tesla rental program, bike share, hovercraft commuter operations, and related amenities) while supporting broader Spaceport Village operations including site amenities and customer service. You will optimize routes, operational practices, and parking systems for the most efficient, safest, and highest-participation transportation program possible. You will train and implement effective customer service strategies, coordinate operations, analyze data, monitor and motivate staff, ensure excellent customer service, engage customers, hire and develop talent, maintain mandatory training, handle scheduling and payroll, and drive process improvements. This role supports the SpaceX mission by delivering efficient transportation logistics, outstanding customer service, vehicle/amenity maintenance, and quality-of-life support that boosts morale and productivity.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Oversee the full portfolio of transportation programs: off-site shuttles (vans and charter buses), on-site shuttle service, Tesla rental program, hovercraft commuter operations, bike share, parking lots/structures/facilities, and related team-building or employee engagement events

• Innovate approaches to increase participation in employee commuter and parking programs through communications, messaging, incentive systems, and creative campaigns

• Act as primary point of contact for parking and transportation facilities; perform strategic analysis to improve and optimize overall system efficiency, routes, and operational practices

• Recommend and support development of internal transportation and parking policies, procedures, and programs

• Lead internal customer relations for commute/transportation questions and feedback; oversee customer service, issue resolution, root-cause analysis, and corrective action plans

• Oversee communication of systems/service changes to stakeholders (email, newsletter, intranet/app, signage, basic graphics)

• Interface with internal stakeholders (including Spaceport Development, Facilities, Culinary, and Hospitality teams) to understand, develop, and align goals

• Monitor quality, consistency, and financial activities of Spaceport transportation and related operations; set/enforce standards, inspect and routinely walk areas of responsibility; strategically drive revenue and improve operating costs

• Train staff on customer service, anticipating guest/employee needs, problem resolution, and safety practices; create and maintain in-person and online training materials; ensure the team is current with all mandatory company training

• Enforce proper safety practices and support high-volume, complex multidisciplinary operations

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

• 3+ years of leadership experience in transportation program management, hospitality, or other corporate employee services programs

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Bachelor’s degree in hospitality or related field

• Experience opening new operations and/or creating operational procedures from the ground up; 1+ years in SpaceX Spaceport Operations a plus

• Advanced knowledge of customer service and problem resolution; excellent written and verbal communication skills

• Experience in a corporate environment; proficient knowledge of human resources management and Microsoft Office/Outlook

• Ability to organize work for large groups in various service formats; strong time management skills

• Experience with high-volume, complex multidisciplinary operations and leading teams of 10+ staff members

• Eye for aesthetic industrial design; ability to read and understand basic floor plans; familiarity with space planning, facilities in an aerospace industry, and ERP software for RFPOs/work orders

• Ability to work effectively in a team environment; make independent judgments with limited information; logical and strategic approach to solving problems

• Communication skills for relaying data (verbally and in writing) between employees, vendors, and customers

• Comfortable working in a high-stress environment balancing several projects, with flexibility to adjust for abrupt changes in strategic direction

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Must be willing to travel to other SpaceX locations for significant/extended periods of time as needed (up to 85% of the time)

• Must be available to work extended hours and weekends

• Must be able to relocate to Starbase, Texas

• Ability to provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies and critical operations

• Valid state issued driver's license
