jobs.title: Engineering Manager, Platform
jobs.description:
ABOUT AIRBYTE:

We’re on a mission to make data available and actionable to everyone, everywhere. With 700+ connectors, our platform powers analytics and gives AI agents the business context they need to do real work. More than 25,000 companies, including 20% of the Fortune 500, rely on Airbyte to put their data to work.


We’re built on open source because we believe companies should have full control over their data. A community of 27K members helps shape what we build, and we’re backed by $181M from investors including Benchmark, Accel, Altimeter, Coatue, and Y Combinator.


Models keep getting better. What holds AI back is the data informing and shaping its decisions, and that's the layer we're building.


We’re just getting started. If you’re excited by big challenges, meaningful ownership, and the chance to help build what’s next, we’d love to meet you.




THE ROLE:

Airbyte is looking for an Engineering Manager, Platform to lead the team responsible for the infrastructure, tooling, and engineering systems that power Airbyte Cloud, Airbyte Flex, and Airbyte Agents.



As an Engineering Manager on the Platform team, you'll lead the engineers responsible for cloud infrastructure, deployment systems, CI/CD, observability, reliability, and the internal tooling that powers engineering velocity across the company. Your work directly shapes both how fast engineers ship and how customers experience Airbyte. This isn't a keep-the-lights-on role. You'll make real tradeoffs between engineering velocity, customer-facing reliability, and long-term architecture every week, and you'll help define how AI transforms the way we build and operate software.



This role combines people leadership, technical strategy, operational excellence, and platform thinking. You'll help define how engineering works at Airbyte - not just what we build.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Lead, mentor, and grow a team of Platform Engineers, Fullstack Engineers, and SREs. Recruit engineers who understand that infrastructure decisions are product decisions.

 - Own the reliability and operational health of Airbyte's production systems.

 - Define the roadmap for Airbyte's platform: infrastructure, CI/CD, deployment automation, observability, internal tooling, and the product surfaces built on top of them.

 - Invest in and drive adoption of AI-powered workflows for debugging, release validation, infrastructure management, and developer productivity, moving past experimentation into real operational leverage.

 - Lead incident response, run blameless postmortems, and ensure systemic fixes follow every outage. Continuously reduce operational toil through automation.

 - Build leverage: a week-long task this year should take ten minutes next year.

 


SUCCESS METRICS:

 - Engineers deploy with confidence and ship faster quarter over quarter.

 - Platform reliability improves as measured by customer-facing SLAs, not just internal dashboards.

 - Operational toil decreases through automation, not heroics.

 - Incidents are detected faster, resolved faster, and the same failure doesn't happen twice.

 - Your team is engaged, growing, and building careers they're proud of.

 


WHAT YOU’LL NEED:

 - 5+ years of software engineering experience, 2+ years managing engineering teams.

 - Experience leading Platform Engineering, Infrastructure, SRE, or Developer Productivity organizations.

 - Strong understanding of cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, observability, and distributed systems.

 - Experience operating production systems at scale.

 - You think about platform work in terms of customer impact, not just engineering elegance.

 - You've navigated the tension between paying down tech debt and shipping product, and you can articulate how you made those calls.

 - Excellent communication skills. You can translate platform strategy into language that product, design, and business leaders understand.

 - You have an insatiable desire to ship.




NICE TO HAVE:

 - Experience with AI-assisted engineering workflows or agentic software development.

 - Experience building internal developer platforms.

 - Familiarity with Terraform, Helm, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, and cloud-native infrastructure.

 - Experience with data infrastructure, ETL/ELT, or large-scale distributed systems.

 - Experience contributing to open-source engineering organizations.

 - Familiarity with Airbyte, connector ecosystems, or developer tooling platforms.

 


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS:

Platform Engineering is the force multiplier for every engineering team at Airbyte.



Your mission is to build the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that enable engineers to move faster while making our platform more reliable, secure, and scalable. Success means every deployment becomes safer, every incident becomes easier to resolve, every engineer becomes more productive, and AI becomes a natural part of how software is built.



The best platform teams are invisible—they make everyone else dramatically more effective. That's the team you'll build.




LOCATION:

 - Onsite 4 days/week in San Francisco, CA




WHY YOU'LL LOVE WORKING AT AIRBYTE:

At Airbyte, we believe great work happens when people feel supported, trusted, and empowered to grow. Our market-leading Total Rewards package is designed to help you thrive professionally and personally. Our benefits and perks include:



• Flexible PTO with a culture that encourages at least 25 days off annually
 • 16 weeks fully paid parental leave for all parents
 • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents
 • 401(k) retirement plan
 • Professional development budget, conference sponsorship, and book reimbursement
 • Commuter benefits and monthly internet reimbursement

 •  Breakfast and lunch in our San Francisco office
 • A collaborative, in-person culture focused on learning, growth, and impact



If you find this role exciting, we encourage you to apply even if you think you don’t meet all of the requirements!



We are not accepting agency submissions or recruiting firm support for this role. Unsolicited resumes will not be considered.



Airbyte is an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, familial status, domestic violence victim status, veteran or military status, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state or local laws. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.



Airbyte is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities in our job application procedures. Please let us know if you need assistance or accommodations due to a disability.

jobs.title: Customer Support Developer (Databases)
jobs.description:
ABOUT AIRBYTE:

We’re on a mission to make data available and actionable to everyone, everywhere. With 700+ connectors, our platform powers analytics and gives AI agents the business context they need to do real work. More than 25,000 companies, including 20% of the Fortune 500, rely on Airbyte to put their data to work.


We’re built on open source because we believe companies should have full control over their data. A community of 27K members helps shape what we build, and we’re backed by $181M from investors including Benchmark, Accel, Altimeter, Coatue, and Y Combinator.


Models keep getting better. What holds AI back is the data informing and shaping its decisions, and that's the layer we're building.


We’re just getting started. If you’re excited by big challenges, meaningful ownership, and the chance to help build what’s next, we’d love to meet you.




THE ROLE:

Are you the kind of developer who gets a rush from cracking a gnarly replication bug, an issue with CDC implementation, or a query that hangs with no obvious reason? Do you thrive at the intersection of writing code and helping customers succeed? As a Customer Support Developer (Databases) at Airbyte, you'll combine hands-on development skills with deep technical empathy to support our growing cloud, embedded, and open-source integration platform. 



This isn't a traditional support role. You'll be writing Java and Kotlin, shipping contributions to our open-source database source and destination connectors, digging into query plans and transaction logs, and directly shaping how customers move mission-critical data between databases, warehouses, and lakes. You'll champion the customer voice alongside our engineering and product teams every day, getting your hands dirty in the code.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Customer Support & Technical Troubleshooting

 - Serve as the primary technical escalation point for database-related customer issues, responding via email, ticketing systems, and video calls with precision and clarity.

 - Triage and prioritize incoming issues with urgency, consistently meeting SLA targets while leveraging AI tools to work smarter and resolve issues faster.

 - Dig into complex issues across relational databases, data warehouses, data lakes, and cloud object storage, not just finding workarounds but partnering with Engineering to root-cause and drive real fixes.

 - Reproduce customer-reported bugs by inspecting connector logs, query plans, replication slots, transaction logs, sync state, and destination table state, and document findings with enough technical detail for Engineering to act on immediately.

 - Support customers through onboarding and troubleshooting for SSH tunnels, network configuration, database user permissions, CDC setup (WAL/binlog/redo logs), and warehouse/lake authentication.



Database Connector Development

 - Get hands-on with customers building and debugging integrations, helping them navigate Airbyte's database sources and destinations with confidence, from authentication and SSL/SSH setup to CDC, schema evolution, incremental cursors, and typed destination tables.

 - Validate database version compatibility across supported engines and releases, maintain testing environments, and reproduce customer-reported behavior on real database and warehouse instances.

 - Support customers writing to data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift), data lakes and object storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, Databricks, Iceberg), and databases (Postgres, MySQL, MSSQL, ClickHouse), including schema evolution and typed-columns behavior.

 - Help customers running database sources (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle, MongoDB, and more) troubleshoot replication behavior, cursor selection, full-refresh vs. incremental vs. CDC trade-offs, and sync state recovery.

 - Contribute directly to Airbyte's open-source database connectors and the Java/Kotlin Bulk CDK: fix bugs, improve error handling, harden schema-evolution and CDC paths, and submit pull requests to the Airbyte repository.

 - Review and test community contributions to database sources and destinations, helping external contributors land high-quality changes.

 - Stay sharp on Airbyte's connector catalog, new database and destination releases, and platform updates so your guidance is always accurate and timely.



Cross-Functional Collaboration & Enablement

 - Be the voice of the customer within Airbyte, working closely with Engineering and Product to surface issues, advocate for feature requests, and ensure customer pain points actually influence the database reliability and performance roadmap.

 - Partner with Solutions Engineering and Sales Engineering to provide white-glove technical onboarding for enterprise customers, including CDC architecture reviews, destination schema modeling, and production readiness assessments.

jobs.title: Head of Fleet and Data
jobs.description:
About Tutor
We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.
Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Fleet and Data to own our robots after they ship: the team that supports them in customers' facilities, the tools that team uses, and the engineering that turns what the fleet sees into a better product.
The job, at its core, is to take work that needs a trained person today and make most of it unnecessary. The team includes the people who support robots in the field day to day, the engineers who build their tools, and the engineers who take on the hard problems from the field. The team writes code, works on hardware investigations, and talks to customers directly.
Much of the team works on customers' schedules. Robots run production in shifts, and the team covers them: support engineers and operators on shift and on call, with shift leads who report to you.
You report to the CTO.

jobs.title: Consultor de Vendas - Oeiras/PI
Operational Excellence Lead
jobs.description:
Location: Remote, New York City, or Oakland, CA

Role Type: Full-time

Compensation: $135,000 or $155,000, depending on seniority

Reports to: Chief Administrative Officer

Visa sponsorship: Not available

Hires remotely in: United States

-

About the Role

The Operational Excellence Lead will connect the organization's long-horizon, cross-functional, and external-facing strategy with internal execution. They will build the operating cadence, information flow, and forums that let the organization run performance-versus-plan at every level, and own the follow-through that keeps decisions and strategy connected across altitudes.

What Success Looks Like

• Leaders know where and why core impact metrics are moving, and how to intervene.

• Forums at every altitude (team level, functional leads, leads review) run with clear owners, decisions, and metrics.

• Operational systems drive high-quality, consistent reporting and better decision-making.

• Resourcing decisions are data-driven, and ROI is tracked over time.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Strategy & Operating Cadence

Own the connective layer between long-term vision and strategy, and functional leads' near-term execution.

• Run performance-versus-plan and OKR processes across the organization, working with leads to define outcomes, metrics, and reporting cadence. Own core planning cycles (e.g., H2 planning) end to end — the calendar, the templates, and the cross-team dependencies.

• Consolidate fragmented ownership, and make ownership, decision-making, and escalation paths explicit.

• Facilitate cross-functional reviews that ladder up into organizational strategy; ask sharp questions, capture action items with clear owners and dates, and enforce time-boxing so discussions actually converge.

• Communicate internally about our impact metric progress by owning the Impact Monthly meeting: build the update deck, and work with teams across the org to source the case studies and highlights that make it concrete.

• Partner with the Director of Talent to create org-wide communications calendar and content based on critical happenings.

Data & Financial Analysis

Ensures the organization has trustworthy, accessible data to run performance-versus-plan, understand unit economics and make resourcing decisions.

• Support the business case for strategic initiatives such as headcount requests, RFPs, or resourcing requests — making the value proposition clear and concrete using business cases, OKRs, or other appropriate value frameworks — before they're resourced.

• Pull and build your own analyses (e.g., in Looker) to diagnose what's driving or blocking core metrics like transitions, usage, CSAT, and launch momentum.

• Use data and diagnosis, not authority, to earn the trust of a highly analytical engineering and impact organization.

Continuous Improvement

Drive better decision making, organizational design and operating orientation using data-driven insights

• Pair alongside individual leaders on specific strategic challenges, both to bolster their output and to diagnose whether a gap is about skills, structure, or hiring.

• Inform performance management and promotions with impact data.

• Maintain a clear view of the organization's critical-path portfolio, including how it breaks down between funded work (what states or customers are paying us for) and unfunded work — a key input into planning and resourcing decisions.

• Continuously improve the operational excellence function's own methodology — refining the templates, tools, and processes it runs on (e.g., the PVP sheet, planning docs, review formats) — and share what's working across teams rather than reinventing it in each forum.

Systems Management

Designs systems to capture and improve our unit economics

• Help define requirements for and implement a revenue operations system.

• Help the organization answer emerging questions about AI and tooling ROI.

• Define clear requirements for measuring cloud costs or personnel costs by state, partnering with an internal engineer or data partner to build the dashboard once the requirements are clear — bringing the finance and business framing that a purely technical build can miss.

Who You'll Work With

You’ll report to the Chief Administrative Officer. Your initial focus is the Impact organization and the Engineering leadership team, together the “core impact apparatus.” You’ll work closely with functional and technical leads across Impact and Engineering and with data and systems teams. Over time, as the role’s scope expands, you’ll also work with leaders in marketing, business development, finance, and people operations.

What We're Looking For

• A senior operator — likely from a product management, product operations or program management background.

• Strong analytical skills and genuine comfort with data: able to pull your own analysis from tools like Looker and build a credible, data-driven case, even without a formal technical or engineering background.

• High emotional intelligence: able to work with senior, strong-willed leaders and get them to take ownership, without dictating to them.

• Excellent synthesis and written communication: able to hold many concurrent threads, re-articulate strategy clearly, and drive high-quality, fast follow-up.

• A bias toward clarity and simplification — comfortable pushing to reduce the number of people involved in a decision or a meeting, not just adding structure.

• Comfortable constructively challenging partners and leaders — willing to stress-test thinking and push back, not just surface issues and let them sit.

• Steady under pressure; this role sits amid a lot of interpersonal complexity and needs someone with strong composure.

• Comfortable operating with significant seniority and scope from day one — this is intended as a senior hire, not an entry point into strategy work.

• Experience in government, public-sector, or B2G contexts, or with mission-driven and nonprofit organizations.

• Experience running OKR or performance-versus-plan processes at scale.

jobs.title: System Administrator (Senior-Level)

jobs.title: CDL Delivery Driver (Pump, Power & HVAC)
jobs.description:
Build the Future with Us — EquipmentShare is Hiring a CDL Delivery Driver

At EquipmentShare, we’re not just filling a role — we’re assembling the best team on the planet to build something that’s never been built before. We’re on a mission to transform an industry that’s been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

Primary Responsibilities

We don’t just deliver equipment - we deliver innovation. At EquipmentShare, our technology ensures that our drivers work efficiently and effectively by providing real-time access to fleet locations, work orders, and delivery details.

• Operates vehicle according to applicable state and federal transportation laws

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

Perks & Benefits

• Competitive compensation

• Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees

• Generous PTO + paid holidays

• Company events, food truck nights, and monthly dinner nights

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

We’re looking for people who:

• See challenges as opportunities

• Embrace change and continuous improvement

• Bring energy, effort, and optimism every day

Skills & Qualifications

Required Skills/Abilities:

• Strong interpersonal and customer service skills with the ability to speak professionally and courteously with customers and staff at delivery points

• Ability to remain focused in a busy environment

Education and Experience:

• Must hold either a commercial drivers license (Class A CDL) or chauffeur’s license depending on state, appropriate for weight of vehicle to be operated

• Must pass background and drug testing as required by federal and/or state department(s) of transportation regulations

• Must pass DOT physical, as trucks driven are over 10k lbs

• Must be at least 21 years old to operate company vehicle

• Must have a clean driving record

Physical Requirements:

• Prolonged periods sitting in a trailer cab for long periods of time

• Must be able to lift and move up to 40 pounds at a time

• Must be able to travel frequently

• CDL drivers may be required to be clean shaven in order to deliver to EquipmentShare customers who have this requirement

• This is a safety sensitive position and any offer of employment will be contingent on passing a 10 panel drug screen

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Optiver is looking for Software Engineers to join our High-Frequency Trading (HFT) team in Austin. Our engineers work at the intersection of research-driven trading, machine learning, ultra-low-latency software and custom hardware to build fully automated trading systems operating across global markets.

As a Software Engineer, you'll work directly with traders, researchers and hardware engineers to solve complex technical challenges, develop new trading strategies and build the systems that bring them to production. Our teams own problems end to end, from data ingestion, feature generation and simulation through to high-performance C++ and FPGA-based execution.

We're continuing to expand into new markets, products and strategies, creating opportunities to build new systems, influence technical direction and see your work directly impact live trading across the world.

What you'll do

• Partner closely with traders and researchers to develop and improve research-driven, machine learning-based trading strategies.

• Build and optimize trading infrastructure across the full lifecycle, from data ingestion, feature generation and simulation through to production execution.

• Solve challenging performance problems across ultra-low-latency C++, software architecture and FPGA-based trading systems.

• Design and develop scalable research infrastructure that enables rapid experimentation, backtesting and deployment of new strategies.

• Push frequent, impactful code changes into production, with direct visibility into their performance in live markets.

• Contribute to the technical direction of our trading systems as we expand into new markets, products and strategies.

• Develop a deep understanding of market microstructure, trading and exchange behavior.

What you’ll get

You’ll join a culture of collaboration and excellence, surrounded by curious thinkers and creative problem-solvers. Motivated by a passion for continuous improvement, you’ll thrive in a supportive, high-performing environment alongside talented colleagues, collectively tackling some of the toughest challenges in the financial markets.

In addition, you’ll receive:

• The opportunity to work alongside best-in-class professionals from over 40 different countries

• A highly competitive compensation package

• Global profit-sharing pool and performance-based bonus structure

• 401(k) match up to 50%

• Comprehensive health, mental, dental, vision, disability, and life coverage

• 25 paid vacation days alongside market holidays

• Extensive office perks, including breakfast, lunch and snacks, regular social events, clubs, sporting leagues and more

Who you are

• Strong engineering instincts and a deep understanding of computer science fundamentals.

• C++ experience preferred, ideally in performance-critical systems such as low-latency trading, market data processing, execution systems or simulation frameworks.

• An interest in solving complex performance challenges, whether through software optimization, systems design or hardware/software integration.

• Innovative, out-of-the-box thinking grounded in real-world pragmatism.

• A desire to continuously improve, learn and solve challenging problems in a rapidly evolving environment.

• Readiness to take ownership, influence technical direction and uphold high engineering standards.

• Experience with Python, Linux, distributed systems or machine learning infrastructure is a plus.

Who we are

Optiver is a tech-driven trading firm and leading global market maker. As one of the oldest market making institutions, we are a trusted partner of 70+ exchanges across the globe. Our mission is to constantly improve the market by injecting liquidity, providing accurate pricing, increasing transparency and acting as a stabilizing force no matter the market conditions. With a focus on continuous improvement, we participate in the safeguarding of healthy and efficient markets for everyone who participates.

Based in ‘The Domain’ neighborhood, Optiver’s Austin office serves as the firm’s innovation nucleus, with a strong focus on quantitative research, software and hardware engineering initiatives. With tech innovation an integral part of our core business, the booming city proved an ideal backdrop for our heavy investment into machine learning, research infrastructure and big data computing. What’s more, with world-class music, food and art scenes, as well as countless scenic outdoor activities, the quality of life for Austin Optiverians is second to none.

Our differences are our edge. Optiver does not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, physical or mental disability, or other legally protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Senior Modeling & Simulation Engineer (TS/SCI)
jobs.description:
K2 is building the largest and highest-power satellites ever flown, unlocking performance levels previously out of reach across every orbit. Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

The rise of heavy-lift launch vehicles is shifting the industry from an era of mass constraint to one of mass abundance, and we believe this new era demands a fundamentally different class of spacecraft. Engineered to survive the harshest radiation environments and to fully capitalize on today's and tomorrow's massive rockets, K2 satellites deliver unmatched capability at constellation scale and across multiple orbits.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

You will build the modeling and simulation capabilities that let us design, verify, and operate spacecraft for demanding national security missions. You will simulate and verify the software that flies and orchestrates some of the largest satellites ever flown, and model how those systems perform against real mission objectives, threats, and operational constraints. As a senior member of the team, you will drive solutions end-to-end across the software stack, make changes to vehicle control software where needed, set technical direction, and mentor other engineers.

In your first 3 months you will generalize our simulation tools to operate in classified contexts, modeling multiple spacecraft and mission profiles, demonstrating robust performance in contested and demanding environments. In your first 6 months you will design many-agent, mission-level simulations and tools for operating entire constellations, directly informing mission assurance and critical company and program decisions.

This role supports classified national security programs. Work is performed on-site in a secure environment and requires an active TS/SCI clearance and US citizenship.

Responsibilities

• Develop mission-level modeling and simulation of national security space missions, capturing operational objectives, environments, and constraints.

• Model and analyze constellation-level capability and performance against mission requirements, including network coverage, beam planning, and resilience in contested environments.

• Support work on classified programs in accordance with all applicable security requirements.

• Create and maintain simulation software infrastructure for our 20kW+ spacecraft.

• Develop physics-based software models of spacecraft subsystems, including propulsion, attitude control, power, and communications systems.

• Create and utilize robust tools to allow for rapid deployment of quality code.

• Perform data analysis and anomaly investigation to identify and resolve on-orbit problems.

• Support integration and testing of spacecraft subsystems.

• Set technical direction, review designs and code, and mentor junior engineers.

Qualifications

• Active U.S. government security clearance (any level), or a clearance held within the last 12 months, and US Citizenship

• Prior experience working on classified national security programs and in secure/SCIF environments, including familiarity with handling classified information and program security protocols.

• Bachelor's degree in physics, aerospace/mechanical/electrical engineering, computer science, math, or a STEM field

• 5+ years of professional modeling and simulation experience.

• Development experience in Rust, C++, or similar compiled language.

• Experience using scientific Python (NumPy, SciPy, etc.), Julia, MATLAB, or similar.

• Demonstrated ability to own complex systems end-to-end and guide the work of other engineers.

Nice to Have

• Master's or PhD in physics, aerospace/mechanical/electrical engineering, computer science, math, or a STEM field.

• Experience with mission-level or campaign-level modeling and simulation for defense or national security applications.

• Facility communicating intuition and expertise effectively to stakeholders.

• Experience working in Rust production environments.

• Experience defining and creating simulation systems.

• Experience with Monte Carlo simulations and probability/statistics.

• Experience with linear algebra, controls, and/or orbital mechanics.

• Experience with space communication modeling (RF, ground stations).

• Basic knowledge of electronics, Linux, and computer architecture.

• Experience with continuous integration and continuous delivery systems.

Compensation and Benefits:

• Base salary range for this role is $160,000 - $200,000 + equity in the company

• Salary will be based on several factors including, but not limited to: knowledge and skills, education, and experience level

• Comprehensive benefits package including paid time off, medical/dental/vision/ coverage, life insurance, paid parental leave, and many other perks

If you don’t meet 100% of the preferred skills and experience, we encourage you to still apply! Building a spacecraft unlike any other requires a team unlike any other and non-traditional career twists and turns are encouraged!

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

Export Compliance

As defined in the ITAR, “U.S. Persons” include U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (i.e., Green Card holders), and certain protected individuals (e.g., refugees/asylees, American Samoans). Please consult with a knowledgeable advisor if you are unsure whether you are a “U.S. Person.”

The person hired for this role will have access to information and items controlled by U.S. export control regulations, including the export control regulations outlined in the International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR). jobs.title: School Nurse
jobs.description:
The School Nurse will work to support the student health needs across the KIPP Nashville school community – either at a designated school or support across multiple schools. S/he will report to the Director of Student Health and in close partnership with the school-based Principal and Director of Operations to prepare for and respond to student and school needs as it relates to student health. Ultimately, our student health team plays a key role in maintaining a safe and healthy environment for KIPP Nashville students.

Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Works to remove, modify, or reduce health-related barriers to learning
• Provides well-student care, health care, first aid, immunizations, and assistance to students at their school; creates a comforting and nurturing environment for ill students
• Provides daily, individual care to students, including but not limited to managing daily medications required by students, administering doctor prescribed medications to students and helping students with physical disabilities
• Advises the Director of Operations and other school staff as needed regarding initiatives, processes, and systems necessary to ensure a healthy school community
• Builds emergency preparedness plans and trains all staff on them to ensure staff school-wide are ready for health emergencies
• Communicates with families around student wellness and health concerns
• Participates in necessary student health events that may occur on non-school days, e.g., New Student Registration
• Performs screenings for scoliosis, vision, hearing, height, weight, and/or other conditions and make referrals and follow-up
• Completes, updates, and maintains student records (accident reports, health records), and completes and submits reports; effectively and efficiently manages the systems for student health paperwork
• Ensures 100% collection of student health documentation for incoming new students
• Maintains physical student health files and ensures they are organized and up-to-date
• Audits student health files annually
• Transfers all health materials and necessary information for student transfers between campuses
• Maintains the security of confidential information
• Collects and maintains student incident forms, ensuring that all applicable parties have documented all pertinent details
• Collaborates with school staff to create and maintain wellness programming to support healthy opportunities for students
• Maintains all mandated COVID protocols and holds staff and students accountable to those health protocols.

Physical Demands

• Minimal Physical exertion required. Generally, the job requires sitting, standing, and walking.
• Light work: exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 10 pounds of force as frequently as needed to move objects
• Possible travel between schools for coverage.

Required Qualifications

Current non-restricted TN Licensure as a Registered Nurse is required. B.S.N. is preferred. 2 years or more in nursing; Current BLS, First Aid, and AED certification; Associate or Nursing Diploma with Pediatric experience, BSN a plus. Licensed or eligible for RN licensure in Tennessee. Experience in a pediatric setting is preferred.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

• Knowledge of evaluation plans and treatment of clients with a variety of illnesses and injuries.
• Ability to apply current nursing research and theory to daily practice.
• Skill in patient care and in the use of medical equipment utilized in the area of assignment.
• Ability to plan and effectively communicate by clearly presenting healthcare-related information and responding to questions from both individuals and groups.
• Ability to develop and maintain positive and productive interpersonal relationships with co-workers, patients, patient families, and school administrators.

Compensation

• The role is paid a competitive hourly rate and is non-exempt from overtime (i.e. eligible for overtime). Pay ranges from $33-$37/hour commensurate with experience. This role includes benefits and will work a 10 month schedule. The schedule is typically Monday through Friday, and is a day shift.
• Robust benefits package including medical, dental, vision, disability, and life insurance policy options. Application for these benefits may be made immediately upon employment. The policy is effective upon the first of the month following the first day of work.
• The vacation package for salaried employees includes 29 paid days throughout the 12 month work schedule (including holidays, fall break, thanksgiving break, winter break). In addition, employees in this role are allotted 6 PTO days. Employees are allotted an additional 2 days after every 2 consecutive years of employment. Eligible staff members receive payment for unused PTO days at the end of the fiscal year.
• Adoption/Parental Caregiver Leave- up to 10 weeks parental leave for the primary caregiver and 2 weeks parental leave for the secondary caregiver paid at 100%.
• Teammates are provided with laptop computers with access to the internet and or email to assist them in performing their job responsibilities.

jobs.title: IT Helpdesk Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT US:

Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.

 


WHO WE ARE:

We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.

 


WHO YOU ARE:

You’re a hands-on IT leader who has built and run help desk teams at fast-growing startups. You know what keeps engineers productive without sacrificing security and compliance. You’re as comfortable configuring a switch or writing an Intune policy as you are coaching a technician or explaining a new control to the team. You’ve worked in regulated environments, and you understand that CMMC, ITAR and EAR aren’t paperwork; they shape how every system is built and used. You take ownership, document what you do, and want to be on-site where the work happens.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Lead, hire and mentor the IT help desk team, and set clear priorities, SLAs and escalation paths

 - Own day-to-day IT support for Windows, macOS and Linux users across the company

 - Administer our Microsoft 365 GCC and GCC High tenants, including identity, email, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams

 - Manage endpoints through Microsoft Intune and Jamf: enrollment, configuration profiles, patching, compliance policies and app deployment

 - Design, maintain and troubleshoot our Ubiquiti and Cisco network infrastructure, including switching, wireless, firewalls and VPN

 - Maintain a CMMC 2.0 compliant environment: implement and monitor controls, collect evidence, and support audits and assessments

 - Ensure IT systems and processes meet ITAR and EAR requirements for handling controlled technical data

 - Manage onboarding and offboarding, access reviews, and asset lifecycle from procurement to disposal

H&M is a part of H&M Group. At H&M Group, we’re determined to create and maintain inclusive, diverse and equitable workplaces throughout our organization. Having a diverse workforce leads to a positive impact on how we address challenges, on what we perceive possible and on how we choose to relate to our colleagues and customers all over the world. Hence, all diversity dimensions are considered in our recruitment process.

H&M Fashion USA, Inc. – Maki Assessment Tool:

We use an online assessment tool called Maki for skills-based selection of applicants for sales advisor positions within some of our stores. Maki is not an automated decision-making tool. Rather, it is a tool that uses an AI-created avatar to present to you a set of multiple-choice questions. These questions are prepared by the H&M hiring team to assess candidates’ ability to perform the duties of the position for which they are applying. The assessment calculates your total score based on predefined point values provided by our H&M team. The hiring team will review your whole application, including your assessment score, to decide whether to advance each candidate to the next stage. Doing the assessment is optional. If you choose to complete the assessment, your score will be one factor that the hiring team considers.

If you have any difficulties or concerns with the online assessment method, you can request an alternative method of assessment by contacting recruitment_support@hm.com. Choosing an alternative method will not affect your chances of being considered for the position, nor does any assessment method provide an advantage or disadvantage in the selection process. You will have the opportunity to provide optional feedback immediately after the assessment and you may always ask questions.

When you take the assessment, we collect your responses and use this information to evaluate your suitability for the role to which you have applied. The answers are saved in your applicant profile. We do not sell the information captured in the questionnaire and do not use any personal information to train any AI models. Our applicant tracking system provider has access to this information but is contractually prohibited from using it for any other purpose.

During this process, we may collect information from you through cookies, with your consent. This may include details such as your electronic network activity information (IP address, timestamps, and device identifiers). This information is accessible to our hiring team but is otherwise kept confidential. For more information, please refer to our Cookie Notice.

We retain this information for 3 years in your applicant file and use it as set forth in our Applicant Privacy Notice. For more information on how your personal data is processed by us, please refer to our Applicant Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Creative Director
jobs.description:
About Cantina:

Cantina is a new social platform founded by Sean Parker with the most advanced AI character creator. Our bots are lifelike, social creatures that can interact wherever people are online—across voice, video, and text. Create yourself, imagine someone new, or choose from thousands of characters to share infinitely scalable, personalized content and seamless group chat.

If you’re excited about how AI can shape creativity and social interaction, come help us build what’s next.



About the Role:
Cantina is looking for a Creative Director to own creative direction across original content, performance advertising, brand campaigns, and product storytelling. This is a hands-on role: you’ll come up with the concept, write the script, generate assets, work through the edit, and keep pushing until it lands.

Some days you’ll direct a small team, and some days you’ll make the whole thing yourself.



What You’ll Do:

 - Own creative direction across original content, performance advertising, brand campaigns, and product storytelling, defining our brand voice and making it recognizable everywhere.

 - Turn product capabilities into concepts people actually want to watch, share, and try for themselves.

 - Recruit and lead a team of 10 to 25 creatives, including creative directors, video editors, motion designers, visual designers, copywriters, screenwriters, producers, and AI filmmakers.

 - Develop and produce video creative for paid social, organic social, product launches, and brand campaigns.

 - Turn a product feature or consumer insight into a great hook, a clear story, and a reason to try Cantina.

 - Write briefs, scripts, and treatments, build storyboards, and direct editors, designers, creators, and AI filmmakers.

 - Make things yourself: cut video, create motion graphics, generate characters and scenes, experiment with voice and sound, and take concepts through to finished assets.

 - Build performance creative testing plans with the growth team, testing concepts, hooks, offers, and calls to action, then using the results to decide what to make next.

 - Develop platform-native creative with the right pacing, framing, captions, and aspect ratios for each placement.

 - Keep a steady pipeline of fresh ideas and turn winning concepts into repeatable formats without running them into the ground.



What You’ll Bring:

 - A strong portfolio of video creative, including performance advertising with measurable results.

 - Great storytelling instincts: you know how to establish a character, create tension, and deliver a payoff in very little time.

 - Hands-on proficiency with video editing and motion design tools.

 - Experience directing small creative teams and giving clear, actionable feedback.

 - An understanding of creative metrics like hook rate, hold rate, CTR, CVR, and CPA, and how to use them to improve the work.

 - Practical experience with AI image, video, and audio production, including the iteration it takes to get a usable result.

 - Speed, taste, and a willingness to try something strange if the idea is good.



Compensation:

The anticipated annual base salary range for this role is between $250,000-$350,000. When determining compensation, a number of factors will be considered, including skills, experience, job scope, location, and competitive compensation market data.

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer, Cameras & CI
jobs.description:
We’re Blue River, a team of innovators driven to create intelligent machinery that solves monumental problems for our customers. We empower our customers – farmers, construction crews, and foresters - to implement safer and more sustainable solutions, driving increased profitability with less reliance on scarce labor. We believe that focusing on the small stuff – pixel-by-pixel and task-by-task - leads to big gains.

Blue River Technology aligns with John Deere’s vision to “innovate on behalf of humanity” by quickly identifying and solving high-value, high-uncertainty challenges in AI, machine learning, computer vision, and robotics. BRT acts as a research and development flywheel, building not only new products but also new platforms that reliably create value for both Deere and its customers. From fully autonomous machines to highly precise farming equipment, BRT and Deere are partnering to create technical breakthroughs in industries like agriculture and construction. Our people are at the heart of what we do. Through cross-disciplinary collaboration, this mission-driven team is eager to define the new frontier of robotics. We are always asking hard questions, rapidly iterating, and getting our boots in the field to figure it out. We won’t give up until we’ve made a tangible and positive impact on the planet!

Blue River Technology is based in Santa Clara, CA.

Summary

We are seeking a highly skilled Embedded Software Engineer to join our team. In this role, you’ll develop embedded software and systems for our computer vision-enabled agricultural products, including the Bay Area’s highest-density compute platform for robotics. Do you thrive in a fast-paced, innovative team environment and get energized about delivering solutions to technical challenges? If so, this role will be an outstanding next step in your career!

• Employment Type: Full-time

• Work Location: Santa Clara, CA

• Visa sponsorship: Available for this position.

Job Responsibilities

• Develop, enhance, and debug new and existing software applications, kernels, and device drivers for impactful robotics computing in C/C++ and Rust within a Linux environment.

• Enhance camera and sensor capabilities, image quality, and exposure configuration; support training data collection operations.

• Ensure OS (Yocto) support is implemented properly for sensors.

• Build automated driver and camera regression tests that run in continuous integration on hardware-in-the-loop platforms.

• Conduct embedded design reviews and code reviews, providing guidance to resolve difficult driver bugs which may require extensive troubleshooting.

• Implement embedded design best practices and methodologies to ensure high performance and reliability, with a strong emphasis on real-time programming considerations.

Required Experience and Skills

• Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or related field.

• 1-3 years of experience developing embedded software.

• Familiarity with cameras/other sensors and camera interfaces (e.g., MIPI CSI-2).

• Strong attention to detail with a focus on testing and continuous integration practices.

jobs.title: Director of Aviation Maintenance Operations, East
jobs.location: Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Florida; Tampa, Florida
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

As Director of Maintenance Operations for the East Region, you will own end-to-end maintenance performance across Zipline’s Regional operations. This is a senior execution role responsible for regional fleet readiness, maintenance systems, staffing, and compliance across multiple distribution hubs and launch sites.

You are not running a single shop. You are building, scaling, and enforcing a maintenance operating model across states, sites, and regulatory contexts. You will set standards, hold leaders accountable, and personally intervene where reliability, safety, or capacity are at risk. Your success is measured in sustained fleet uptime, audit-ready systems, and the ability to scale without surprises.

This role sits at the center of Zipline’s next phase of operational maturity in the US.

What You'll Do

• Own Regional Maintenance Performance. You are accountable for maintenance outcomes across your region, including organizational financial performance, fleet asset allocations, system uptime and capacity, deferred maintenance risk, parts availability, and recovery from incidents or systemic issues.

• Lead and Develop Site-Level Leaders. Build, manage, and coach Heads of Maintenance or equivalent leads at each site. Set clear expectations, review performance rigorously, promote ownership and drive accountability, and upgrade talent when needed.

• Design and Enforce Maintenance Systems. Own regional maintenance systems including preventive and corrective maintenance programs, tooling standards, documentation, training programs, scheduling, and escalation paths. Ensure consistency without slowing local execution.

• Drive Reliability at Scale. Anticipate failure modes before they impact operations. Use data, trend analysis, and field insight to prioritize fixes, allocate resources, and prevent repeat issues across sites. Create and execute fleet upgrade and retrofit plans while balancing uptime and resource utilization.

• Ensure Safety and Regulatory Excellence. Maintain audit-ready compliance across all states and regulatory environments. Own traceability, record quality, and adherence to internal and external requirements. Step in personally for audits, findings, or serious incidents.

• Partner Cross-Functionally at the Regional Level. Work closely with Flight Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Business Operations to resolve systemic issues, influence design and policy, and align capacity to demand.

• Support Launches and Expansion. Lead maintenance readiness for new site launches and expansions in the region, including staffing models, tooling, spares strategy, and early-life reliability.

What You'll Bring

• 10+ years leading maintenance or technical operations in aerospace, aviation, robotics, or other high-reliability hardware environments.

• Proven experience owning outcomes across multiple sites or regions, not just a single operation.

• Strong systems thinker who can balance standardization with local execution realities.

• Demonstrated ability to build leaders, not just teams, and hold them accountable to measurable results.

• Comfortable operating in high-tempo, ambiguous environments where judgment matters more than process purity.

• Technical background in mechanical, electrical, or aerospace systems strongly preferred. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required.

• Willingness to travel frequently across your region with hands-on presence at critical moments.

What Else You Need To Know

The starting cash range for this role is $160,00.00 - $180,000,00. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. The total compensation package for this role may also include: equity compensation; overtime pay; discretionary annual or performance bonuses; sales incentives; benefits such as medical, dental and vision insurance; paid time off; and more.

jobs.title: Phlebotomist / Administrative Assistant (Extended Hours)
jobs.description:
About Us

One Medical is a primary care solution challenging the industry status quo by making quality care more affordable, accessible and enjoyable. But this isn’t your average doctor’s office. We’re on a mission to transform healthcare, which means improving the experience for everyone involved - from patients and providers to employers and health networks. Our seamless in-office and 24/7 virtual care services, on-site labs, and programs for preventive care, chronic care management, common illnesses and mental health concerns have been delighting people for the past fifteen years.

In February 2023 we marked a milestone when One Medical joined Amazon. Together, we look to deliver exceptional health care to more consumers, employers, care team members, and health networks to achieve better health outcomes. As we continue to grow and seek to impact more lives, we’re building a diverse, driven and empathetic team, while working hard to cultivate an environment where everyone can thrive.

The Opportunity

As a One Medical Flex Lab Service Specialist/Member Support Specialists at one of our offices, you’ll provide an exceptional experience for our patients and help them accomplish an important part of their care journey by providing venipuncture as well as other clinical support services. You will be an ambassador for patients, with a mastery of human connection and a strong drive for service. You will remove barriers to care, resulting in a truly exceptional in-office patient experience. You are the steward of the space and ensure the look and feel of the office lobby are on brand with the One Medical experience. You will be the first point of contact for our patients, as well as provide any other support as requested by the Practice Coordinators, Operations Manager, or providers.  Our Flex Lab Service Specialist/Member Support Specialists support multiple offices in a Market.

You are a strong team player and use your innovative problem solving skills to tackle various tasks and challenges. You combine excellent specimen collection technique with tactful interpersonal skills during every interaction with your patients, at both the front desk and in the lab. You have a strong grasp of verbal and written communication. You are able to identify opportunities and deliver on customer-centric solutions while using empathy, focus, and compassion in all interactions with patients and teammates. You bring self-awareness to your daily work to utilize your strengths and develop your areas of opportunity. You thrive in cultures that focus on feedback and growth and are nimble in their approach to respond to the needs of the patients and team. You have an unwavering drive to help and serve others and create amazing moments for our members and teammates. If this sounds like you, we would love to connect.

What you’ll likely work on:

• Use impeccable C-I-CARE (a framework containing the key elements of a great interaction and effective communication that we use with patients and each other) in all patient interactions, both clinical and administrative, and ensure a fluid and positive in-office experience through patient intake, same day schedule management, appropriate follow up scheduling, strong knowledge of billing and insurance, monitoring patient feedback and assisting with outreach as necessary

• Provide best in class venipuncture services on a population ranging from pediatrics to geriatrics, depending on the office location

• Perform and assist with extended scope duties such as, but not limited to non-blood specimen collection, EKGs/ECGs, vitals

• Maintain high standards of in-office care through proper specimen labeling, handling and processing, inventory upkeep, and tool sterilization

• Continue to care for our members beyond the lab room by answering patient messages, following up on lab cases and assisting our providers and virtual medical team with clerical duties such as, but not limited to biometric screening forms, medical record and consult review, billing inquiries, and DOH reporting

• All front of house duties including check in/check out, insurance verification, printing/paperwork tasks, prepping tests, tasking to service level expectations etc

• Contribute to team development through rounding, attending team huddles, participating in team problem solving, supporting in office providers with ad hoc asks, etc.

• Perform opening and closing duties/daily office upkeep as required, including maintaining the look and feel of both patient and employee facing spaces, restocking supplies, and organization

• Master our technology suite including, but not limited to Slack, G-suite, Zoom, Circulation, RingCentral, and our Electronic Medical Record System, in order to interact with team members and complete daily work

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification.  They are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of job duties performed by personnel in this classification.  Other job related duties may be assigned by management.

What you’ll need:

• At least 6 months of direct phlebotomy experience performing venipuncture and capillary collections outside of a training/externship environment

• Strong customer service skills, including ability to establish and maintain effective customer relationships and deliver customer-centric solutions

• Strong written and verbal communication skills

• A High School Diploma or equivalent

• Proficiency in computer technology such as typing, navigating the internet and using multiple software systems simultaneously

• Experience working on collaborative, diverse, multi-disciplinary teams (additional experience with remote teams a plus)

• A proven ability to display confidence and instill trust during the collection process while delivering individualized, human-centered, customer-focused care

• A proven track record of persisting through change, consistently stepping up to take action on challenges, and learning quickly and effectively when faced with new situations or tasks

The range for this role is $25.75 to $27.75 per hour based on a standard full-time schedule, with a 1.25 differential for eligible extended hours.   Total compensation packages may be based on factors unique to particular candidates, such as skill sets, depth of experience, and work location. The total compensation package for this position may also include benefits. For more information, visit https://www.onemedical.com/careers/

This is a full time role (40 hrs/week) with 8 hr shifts generally taking place Monday - Wednesday, Saturday - Sunday between between 7:30am - 7:00pm at our offices in New York, NY & Brooklyn, NY.  Flex Flex Lab Service Specialist/Member Support Specialists lend support to multiple One Medical locations in a market and location and schedule are subject to change.

One Medical offers a robust benefits package designed to aid your health and wellness.  All regular team members working 24+ hours per week and their dependents are eligible for benefits starting on the team member's date of hire:

Taking care of you today

• Paid sabbatical for every five years of service

• Free One Medical memberships for yourself, your friends and family

• Employee Assistance Program - Free confidential services for team members who need help with stress, anxiety, financial planning, and legal issues

• Competitive Medical, Dental and Vision plans

• Pre-Tax commuter benefits

• PTO cash outs - Option to cash out up to 40 accrued hours per year

Protecting your future for you and your family

• 401K match

• Credit towards emergency childcare

• Company paid maternity and paternity leave

• Paid Life Insurance - One Medical pays 100% of the cost of Basic Life Insurance

• Disability insurance - One Medical pays 100% of the cost of Short Term and Long Term Disability Insurance

In addition to the comprehensive benefits package outlined above, practicing clinicians also receive

• Malpractice Insurance - Malpractice fees to insure your practice at One Medical is covered 100%.

• UpToDate Subscription - An evidence-based clinical research tool

• Continuing Medical Education (CME) - Receive an annual stipend for continuing medical education

• Rounds - Providers end patient care one hour early each week to participate in this shared learning experience

• Discounted rate to attend One Medical’s Annual REAL primary care conference

One Medical is an equal opportunity employer, and we encourage qualified applicants of every background, ability, and life experience to contact us about appropriate employment opportunities.

One Medical participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.  Please refer to the E-Verification Poster and Right to Work Poster for additional information.

Your work schedule could be subject to change based on business direction at any time.

jobs.description:
About Cantina:

Cantina is a new social platform founded by Sean Parker with the most advanced AI character creator. Our bots are lifelike, social creatures that can interact wherever people are online—across voice, video, and text. Create yourself, imagine someone new, or choose from thousands of characters to share infinitely scalable, personalized content and seamless group chat.

If you’re excited about how AI can shape creativity and social interaction, come help us build what’s next.




About the Role:

Cantina is looking for a Video Content Strategist and Editor to lead our outbound video marketing, driving consumer growth and retention, creator adoption, and brand awareness. You’ll turn Cantina’s vast video output from creators, product and engineering announcements, and thought leadership into scroll-stopping video that shows why the best content and creators are on Cantina.




What You’ll Do:

 - Review Cantina’s most successful and high profile content to find videos to amplify or excerpt from for supercuts and promotional videos

 - Piece together clips to create a consistent stream of supercuts showing off Cantina’s best content, biggest creators, most powerful capabilities, and latest features

 - Review new feature releases, conceptualize explainer and example videos, shoot, and publish

 - Lead conceptualization, scripting, shooting, and editing for executive talking head content
   



What You’ll Bring:

 - High taste and ruthless standards for quality, with the ability to rapidly scan huge volumes of video and pull out the best clips.

 - Absurdly fast editing skills, using the latest tools to produce high-quality video daily.

 - Virality instincts: you’re up on the latest formats and tactics and can predict and produce highly performant content.

 - Creative strategy skills to translate high-level concepts and instruction into brilliant content ideas.



Nice To Have:

 - Experience developing, producing, and publishing a viral video media property or a daily/weekly recurring format.

 - Time as lead short-form video strategist for a top 20 global creator.

 - Former successful off-screen solo video creator/curator.

 - Scrappy lead video producer stints at a forward-thinking consumer tech brand.



Compensation:

The anticipated annual base salary range for this role is between $155,000-$175,000. When determining compensation, a number of factors will be considered, including skills, experience, job scope, location, and competitive compensation market data.



Benefits:

 - Competitive salary and generous company equity

 - Medical, dental, and vision insurance – 99.99% of premiums covered by Cantina

 - 401(k) retirement savings plan

 - Complimentary lunch and snacks for in-office employees

 - One Medical membership, and more!

jobs.title: Associate/Senior Associate - Private Equity
jobs.description:
We are global private markets specialists delivering tailored investment solutions, advisory services, and impactful, data driven insights to the world’s investors. Leveraging the power of our platform and our peerless intelligence across sectors, strategies, and geographies, we help identify the advantages and the answers our clients need to succeed.

Position Overview

This role will engage broadly across private equity, with a focus on co-investments and primary fund investments. The Associate/Senior Associate will take meaningful ownership across the investment process, including sourcing, screening, due diligence, underwriting, Investment Committee preparation, execution and ongoing portfolio monitoring. The individual will be expected to drive workstreams forward, develop independent investment perspectives, identify key areas of risk and opportunity, and translate analysis into clear recommendations for senior team members and Investment Committee discussions. The role is well suited for an investment professional with a go-getter mindset who can operate with increasing autonomy, manage multiple priorities and take accountability for high-quality execution in an entrepreneurial, collaborative and low-ego culture characterized by high volume and a fluid structure. The successful candidate should be able to evaluate individual opportunities while also thinking like a portfolio manager, considering how co-investments and fund commitments work together within a broader portfolio and how exposures across managers, industries, geographies and stages affect portfolio construction.

Essential Job Functions:

• Take ownership of key workstreams across the sourcing, screening, due diligence, underwriting and execution of private equity co-investments and primary fund investment opportunities, leveraging the firm’s global network

• Evaluate and analyze buyout co-investment transactions across industries and geographies, as well as primary fund opportunities across managers, strategies, sectors and regions

• Assess private equity managers and funds, including team capabilities, investment strategy, track record, portfolio construction, market positioning, alignment of interests and key terms

• Lead and coordinate elements of the due diligence process, working with fund managers, company management teams, investment bankers, advisors and internal teams to identify key investment considerations, identify new opportunities and move co-investments and primary fund commitments toward a decision

• Develop financial and investment analyses, including valuation, leveraged buyout and cash flow analysis, as appropriate, and evaluate underlying assumptions, sensitivities and risk/reward considerations

• Take ownership of the preparation and presentation of due diligence materials and Investment Committee memoranda for both co-investments and primary fund investments

• Develop an independent investment perspective, synthesize complex quantitative and qualitative information into clear conclusions and recommendations, and confidently communicate and defend that position in team discussions and Investment Committee meetings

• Coordinate transaction execution, closing and structuring for co-investments and fund commitments, proactively identifying and helping resolve issues throughout the execution process; monitor existing investments and fund relationships, evaluate performance and material developments, and maintain relationships with private equity sponsors, intermediaries, advisors and other investors

• Represent the firm professionally in external interactions and contribute to broader portfolio and market discussions by identifying themes, trends and potential investment opportunities across managers, strategies and sectors

• Support the development of junior team members by reviewing work, sharing investment perspectives and providing guidance as appropriate to level

Education and/or Work Experience Requirements:

• 2-4+ years of private equity experience, preferably including co-investments and/or primary fund investing, or other relevant investment experience

• Demonstrated experience evaluating private equity investments, with transaction execution experience and exposure to manager, fund and track-record analysis preferred

• Strong quantitative and financial modeling skills, with the ability to assess valuation, investment returns and sensitivities

• Strong sense of risk/reward trade-offs and an ability to display sound investment judgment

• Self-starter with the ability to independently structure analysis, identify the most important diligence questions, “work a deal” and think “outside the box” when evaluating and progressing opportunities

• Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to synthesize detailed analysis into concise, decision-useful recommendations and communicate and present ideas effectively, both verbally and in writing

• Capable of managing multiple concurrent priorities, with strong attention to detail and a high degree of accountability for deliverables

• Promote and demonstrate a positive, team-oriented attitude, with a desire to develop, coach and lead deal teams as experience and responsibility increase

Other Attributes:

• Fluent written and spoken English

• CFA and/or MBA a plus, but not a requirement

• Demonstrated ownership mentality and willingness to take initiative beyond assigned tasks

• Strong judgment and comfort operating in a fast-paced environment with evolving priorities

• Collaborative, low-ego approach with the ability to work effectively across seniority levels and functions

Salary Range: $122,000 - $180,000

The salary range is an estimate of pay for this position.  Actual pay may vary depending on job-related factors that can include location, education, skill, and experience.  The salary range does not include any benefits or other forms of possible compensation that may be available to employees.
